**The Master Skills button opens the Master Skills page again.** On the Enhanced Plus Stats page it was showing the Character page instead.
**New: Doors in the Decorate catalogue.** Daggerfall's own interior doors can be hung in any open doorway of your home, house or ship. Choose one and press Place.

While you place a door, **every free doorway is marked** in green and the one you are looking at in gold. The door fits itself into the doorway you look at, sized to the opening. Turn it to swing it the other way.
A door hangs only in a doorway it can close. If the free doorways are all too wide for it (an arch), the bar says so.
A door you hung stays open, shut or locked as you left it, and you can move it within its doorway on any later visit.
The bar tells you how many doorways are free, or that the house has none. The catalogue says the same before you choose a door.
A placed door opens and shuts like the room's own doors, blocks the way while shut, and is shared with everyone in the room.
A door parts the rooms on either side of it, so a house with an open doorway becomes two rooms for the room tabs (and for renting, below).

**New: Rooms to rent.** In a home with more than one room, the Decorate panel has a "Rooms to rent" tab. Choose a room, set its price in gold a day (-100, -10, +10, +100), and offer it. Change the price whenever you like; a tenant keeps what they paid for.

**New: Rooms to rent.** In a home with more than one room, the Decorate panel has a "Rooms to rent" tab. Choose a room, set its price in gold a day (-100, -10, +10, +100), and offer it. Change the price whenever you like; a tenant keeps what they paid for.
Other players see "Rent a room: from N gold a day" at your door. They choose a room and how many days (1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 real days), see the price, and confirm.
A tenant can walk into your home whoever else you let in, and may rest there. They can't open your cupboards, drop items or cast spells.
The rent waits at your home. Collect it from "Rooms to rent" whenever you like; it goes into your bank account in that region.
"Stop offering" takes a room off the market. A tenant who has already paid stays until their days run out, and can't renew it. Once they have gone, "Clear it" takes the room off your list.
A home can't be sold while someone rents a room in it. Rent you never collected is paid with the sale.
You can rent up to 3 rooms at once, and renew your own room from its door while it is still offered.

**New: Exterior.** Stand outside your own home and press Decorate. The "Exterior" tab paints the walls, windows, roof and door with Daggerfall's own looks: walls and windows in any of ten building styles (manor, tavern, temple, village and more) and four climates; the roof and door in four climates and six styles.
Each choice is shown on your house as you pick it. "Paint it" keeps it for everyone to see; leaving the tab puts back anything you did not paint.
Winter still snows on your roof. Painting is free.
**New: decorate outside your home.** Stand on your own lot and press Decorate to place catalogue pieces outside, priced as they are inside.

**Your lot** is the ground around your house. Its edge is marked while you place a piece. A piece must stand wholly on it: one that reaches past its edge, into the house or onto a neighbour's ground can't be placed, and the bar says why.
Up to 60 pieces a yard. Everyone walking the street sees them.
Outside, pieces hold nothing and give no light, and doors are for doorways only.

**Your Lycanthropy spell is free from the hotbar**, just like it is when you cast it from the spellbook. Before, the hotbar (and the diamond's spell key) charged 5 spell points, and with an empty pool it refused with "You don't have the spell points."
**The hotbar is now on by default.** Ten slots sit above your health bars on keys 1 to 0. Fill them by dragging items from your pack and spells from your spellbook.
**Prefer the diamond?** Set Features > Interface > Quick slots to Diamond. If you had turned quick slots Off, they stay off.
The Warden's fight now crosses three courts and ends in a wipe you have to break.
**His aspect and trials show under his health bar**, each with its icon and what it does.
**A card shows tonight's marks before the fight**: beside the gate's countdown in the street, and again as you step into the court. It lists how to deal with each one.
**Two new courts, the same size as the first.** At each phase change he bounds across the sea of fire to the next one.
**A walkway rises out of the fire behind him**, stone by stone, so you can follow. He waits under his ward until someone crosses, then opens the new phase.
He only targets fighters in his court, and **he can only be struck from his court** too: blows and spells from a walkway or a court he has left don't land. Don't get left behind.
In the last court he calls **Dagon's Reckoning** from its centre every minute or so. It lands on the whole arena, and nothing resists it.
**Crystals of Oblivion grow across the floor** while he calls it: 3 to 8, depending on how many of you are there. **Break every one** before it lands.

Break them all and the Reckoning fails. **He is stunned for 8 seconds, and every hit on him deals 50% more.** The crystals must break before its last half second: a crystal struck later doesn't count.

Break them all and the Reckoning fails. **He is stunned for 8 seconds, and every hit on him deals 50% more.** The crystals must break before its last half second: a crystal struck later doesn't count.
The boss bar counts the crystals left and the seconds remaining. The chat names whoever breaks each one.

**Burning ground now hits harder**, and you can feel it: the edge of the screen glows in the ground's colour while you stand in it, flares when it burns you, and a warning tells you to step out. You also hear it hiss when you step in.
**He hits harder**: every attack deals about a third more. Two heavy hits in a row will kill you if you haven't healed.

**Clearer telegraphs**: a sharp edge you can read from anywhere, a fuse that burns around the rim as the wind-up runs down, faster pulsing as it's about to land, a texture showing what it is (fire, frost, lightning, venom), and a shockwave when it hits.
**Impacts throw sparks and debris**, and you can **see the Meteor fall** out of the sky onto its target.
**Your loot spreads out** when he falls. Each piece flies in its own direction across a wide arc toward you and lands at least a metre from the others, instead of in one heap.
**Nothing falls off the edge.** Every piece lands on the court's floor, however close to the edge he died.
**Look at a piece to inspect it**: its name and rarity show under your crosshair, with its stats in quick loot. The gold shows how much it is.
**Press activate to pick it up**, like any loot pile. Walking over it still works too.
His chest bursts in gold as the spoils leave it, and each piece sparks in its rarity's colour where it lands (brighter for Rare and up).
**The Sigil Broker sells two new pieces**, listed under the day's stock as **Insignia**. They belong to your account: buy once, and every character on it can wear them.
**Gatebreaker** (30 Sigil Stones): a new title, worn over your name in the colours of a Gate's fire.
**Dagon's Fire** (50 Sigil Stones): an **aura**, a ring of fire that circles the ground where you stand. Flames lick up out of it and embers wheel around it, and every player near you sees it.

**They are expensive on purpose.** Each Gate you help close drops one Sigil Stone, so the title takes about thirty Gates and the aura about fifty. Your account has to have closed enough Gates to pay the price, not only carry the stones.
**Wear them or take them off** from the Broker's window or your account card. Your own aura lights at once, and other players see it from your next step into a new area.
You need to be signed in with a username and password to buy insignia; guest accounts can't keep them.

**Much smoother with lots of players around** when you use the Morrowind bodies. Players outside your view are no longer animated and drawn every frame, the bodies near you share the work across frames, and a crowd milling around you no longer makes the game rebuild bodies over and over (the main cause of the stutter).
When a nearer player takes over a body slot from a farther one, it now waits a moment instead of swapping constantly, and a player wearing the same look reuses a body that was just freed instantly.
**Fish with the net.** Carry a **Fishing-Net**, stand in water, swim, or stand at sea, by daylight (07:00-17:59). A prompt appears: **Cast the net**.
**Hold E** to wind the net, then let go to throw it. The longer you hold, the farther it goes (3 to 12 metres).
**Wait** for a bite. The fish bite faster in the first and last hours of daylight, and slower in a thunderstorm.
**When the floats dip, press E** (or attack) straight away. On a phone with haptics on, it buzzes.
**Haul it in:** hold E to raise the band, let go to lower it. Keep the net's weight inside the band until the net is full.
**What you catch:** 1-2 Raw Fish go to your Stores. The message names the fish, for example *"+2 Largemouth Bass, as Raw Fish"*.
A **full net** gives more.
A missed tug or a slipped net still gives a plain catch, never nothing.

**Schools:** two schools rise in the water of each area every day. You'll see the fish on the surface, or the prompt tells you where, for example *"a school rises 14 m north"*. Cast into one for an extra fish.
**At sea:** on ground other players have confirmed, you can sometimes catch a **Pearl** (1 in 50) or a **Slaughterfish** (1 in 100). A Slaughterfish gives its scales and an extra fish.
**Trophies:** about 1 haul in 200 brings up a trophy fish, which goes straight into your pack.
**Daily limit:** 40 hauls a day per account.

**XP follows your rank.** Each haul gives XP as if it were the highest tier your rank has unlocked. Fishing now levels like the other gathering skills: a Novice earns 15 XP a haul, a rank 55 angler 75.

**Specialisations:** Angler (a longer tug window) and Netter (+2 fish from a school, not +1) at 50; Deep-Sea (the sea's Pearl and Slaughterfish chances doubled) and Pearl Diver (Pearl chance tripled) at 100.

**Specialisations:** Angler (a longer tug window) and Netter (+2 fish from a school, not +1) at 50; Deep-Sea (the sea's Pearl and Slaughterfish chances doubled) and Pearl Diver (Pearl chance tripled) at 100.

**The Professions page** now lists Fishing as practised, shows your hauls today, and explains how to fish.
Pearls can be withdrawn from your Stores as Daggerfall's own Pearl, and sold on the market.
Fishing doesn't work in dungeons or settlements. If you can't fish yet, the prompt tells you why.

**Trade in gold or Drakes.** You can now price a listing in **gold** as well as Drakes. On the Market tab, switch between **Drakes** and **Gold** next to the filters in Materials, Crafted and History. Each view shows one currency at a time.

**Buying with gold.** The gold comes out of your purse first, then your letters of credit, then your bank account in the region of the board you're using. You always pay exactly the price shown. If the purchase is refused, the gold goes straight back.
**Selling for gold.** In **My listings**, choose **Priced in gold** when you list a Stores material or a crafted piece.
There's no fee to list. Each sale pays 1% plus the usual 5% tax out of its price.
Your gold is held for you until you collect it. Press **Collect into your bank here** under My listings, and it goes into your account at that board's bank.
**Couriers** cost 10 gold for every Drake a Drakes courier would charge.
Buy orders, auctions and commissions are still in Drakes.
Gold trading is for characters of the online realm. Other characters see the Drakes market as before.

**Materials bought with gold** show in your Stores as "bought with gold". You can withdraw them to your pack or sell them again for gold. They can't be used at a Forge, Workbench or Loom, in a craft, for a Court or guild writ, in the guild Stores, to fill a buy order, or sold for Drakes.
**A piece bought with gold** can only be listed again for gold.
**Goods bought with Drakes** can only be sold again for Drakes.
A character whose sales are holding gold can't be deleted until the gold is collected.
Materials and pieces you gathered or made yourself can be sold for either currency.

**New key: the Down arrow opens your Professions and Stores** on either UI skin. Before, these pages were only on the Enhanced pause menu, so classic-skin players online couldn't see their ranks or take gathered goods out of their Stores. At a ship's helm the Down arrow still lowers sail, and the Up arrow still raises it. You can rebind the key in Settings → Controls, under Professions.

**Shop and home stations work on the classic skin.** The Forge, Workbench and Loom in shops, and the stations in your own home, now open the Stores page on either skin. Classic-skin players can also buy the Forge, Workbench and Loom for their homes.
Your first harvest each session tells you which key opens your Stores.
Offline, the key tells you that your professions are kept online.

**New loggers can chop in every forest.** Pine, the tree a Novice can fell, used to grow only in the mountains. The Woodlands, Haunted Woodlands and Swamps had only Oak, which needs Logging 10, and Rainforests and Subtropical lands usually had no tree you could fell at all. Now about 2 trees in 5 in those forests are Pine, so you can start Logging wherever you live.
Court writs can now ask for Pine Logs in those regions.

Using a Repair Kit or a Field Repair Kit from your inventory now asks **which piece to mend** whenever more than one piece could use it. You no longer have to drop your loot to get a kit onto the sword you care about.

**Classic inventory:** a list pops up with each weapon or armour piece and how worn it is, for example `Iron Longsword 42% (worn)`. Double-click a row or pick it with the arrow keys and Enter. Click outside the list to keep the kit.
**Enhanced inventory:** a "Mend which?" window lists the same pieces. Click one to mend it, or press **Keep** (or Escape) to keep the kit.
The pieces you're wearing come first, then the rest of your pack, each group most worn first. `(worn)` marks the ones you have on.
A kit used from a hotbar or quickslot can't ask, so it now mends **what you're wearing first**, then the pack, instead of whatever happened to be most worn.
**Kits no longer mend arrows.** Arrows always counted as the most worn weapon, so Field Repair Kits and Iron Repair Kits were spent on the quiver.
A kit used from a corpse or a chest now mends your own gear, not the other items in that pile.
The boss music is louder and darker.
**The fight's music is much louder**: about 10 dB up in his first phase and 7 dB in the rest, well above the dungeon music it replaces.
**It still never clips**, even at the highest music volume.
**No more bouncy plucked strings.** A low, driving brass figure pushes each phase instead.
**A villain's harmony**: the fight moves between D minor and B-flat minor, with the bright major chords taken out.
**New themes for the Warden** on low brass, built on grinding half steps where the old ones climbed to a fanfare.
**Heavier drums**: low drums and toms in place of the hi-hat and tambourine.
**A bell tolls low** at each section, and in his wrath it tolls the tritone.
The music still grows with each phase, and **his fall still ends on its triumphant fanfare**, now louder too.
Fixes and improvements.

**"This character's save is too big for the realm to take" is fixed for any normal save.** An online character's save had grown past the 4 MB the realm accepted in one piece, and every save after that was refused.
**Online saves are now compressed** before they go to the realm, usually to a small fraction of their size. The realm takes saves up to 16 MB before compression.
Trades, guild deposits, houses and decor all work with the bigger saves too.
An older copy of the game still reads the same character correctly. It just can't save one that has grown this big: update to keep playing it.
**Harbours come alive.** Port towns now have ships moored along their shore, sails stowed. Every player in the port sees the same ships in the same berths.
**Ships come and go.** A moored ship stays a while, then sets sail, clears the harbour mouth and heads out to sea. Merchantmen sail in from the sea and tie up at a free berth.

**Everyone has a purpose.** Near a port, merchantmen are coming or going, navy ships patrol the harbour approaches, and pirates lurk offshore waiting for merchants. Follow a merchant and she'll lead you to port.
**Ships steer round the coast.** They find their way round headlands and into harbours instead of running at the shore, and use their sweeps to get in or out when the wind is against them.
**A fight still comes first.** A navy ship at her berth will sail out to meet a pirate, and a merchant will flee. Once the fight is over, she heads back to her berth.
**Fixed: an empty sea online.** Sailing out while a friend was still in town could leave you with no ships at all at sea. The sea now fills around whoever is actually on the water.

**Faster zoom at the helm.** The mouse wheel zooms in and out at the helm much more quickly: from first person to framing your whole ship in about a dozen notches, instead of scrolling for ages before it picked up speed. On foot nothing changes.

**Everything from one menu.** Look at any part of your own boat and its options appear under the crosshair, like the loot list: Take the helm, Board, Open storage, Pick up, Change style, Status and Position (whichever your boat has). Scroll the mouse wheel or the d-pad to choose, and press activate. On the hull nothing is picked until you scroll, so a stray click on your deck does nothing. The menu stays out of the way while you're at the helm.

Scroll the mouse wheel or the d-pad to choose, and press activate. On the hull nothing is picked until you scroll, so a stray click on your deck does nothing. The menu stays out of the way while you're at the helm.

**Your old habits still work.** Looking right at the helm, the chest or the ladder lights that option first, so a single press does what it always did (the ladder you look at is the one you board at). In Steal mode the helm lights "Pick up", and switching mode switches it back.
**No more guessing why.** An option you can't use right now is shown with the reason, such as "Pick up (at her helm)" or "Pick up (passengers aboard)". Ships from a deed can't be picked up.
**No more guessing why.** An option you can't use right now is shown with the reason, such as "Pick up (at her helm)" or "Pick up (passengers aboard)". Ships from a deed can't be picked up.
**On a phone, with the classic interface, or indoors,** tap or click the boat's hull to get the same options as a list.

**Your plunder no longer vanishes.** If you fast travel or go through a door before emptying a captured ship's hold, or before picking up the floating casks from a ship you sank, your crew stows it all in your boat's hold first (or your pack, and it tells you if anything wouldn't fit). Casks still sink a couple of minutes after a ship goes down, so don't sail off and leave them. (Casks from ships someone else sank are still theirs.)

**Boats left in dungeons stay.** A boat you place underground is now kept when you leave, along with everything in its hold, and waits for you in that dungeon. Before, it was destroyed and its cargo lost. You can turn this back off in Come Sail Away's settings (Compatibility).

**Boats left in dungeons stay.** A boat you place underground is now kept when you leave, along with everything in its hold, and waits for you in that dungeon. Before, it was destroyed and its cargo lost. You can turn this back off in Come Sail Away's settings (Compatibility).

**Harbours are sturdier.** Towns on an isthmus or a peninsula keep their harbour, a port whose coast hadn't loaded yet finds its harbour a moment later, and ships no longer try to sail through a spit or a breakwater into a berth.

**Harbours are sturdier.** Towns on an isthmus or a peninsula keep their harbour, a port whose coast hadn't loaded yet finds its harbour a moment later, and ships no longer try to sail through a spit or a breakwater into a berth.

**Ships don't get stuck.** A ship blocked by a wreck on her way into a berth takes another berth. A ship that can't find a way round a long headland goes about her own business instead of running at the shore. Pirates lurk and navy ships patrol on open water, not on the beach.

**Ports look the same for everyone online.** Moored ships no longer depend on your character's level, a friend's moored ships no longer empty your sea, and sailing a little way out and back no longer empties the harbour.
**Gamepad steering at the helm** is no longer taken over by the boat menu when you look down at your deck.
**Zoom at the helm** now moves on the first notch when your ship's rigging is in the way, and a trackpad swipe no longer rushes through the whole range.

**You can no longer be left alive at 0% health.** Dying while a window was open over the death (talking to a temple priest in a building, for one) could close the death screen and leave you walking at 0% health, unable to die again - and then free to buy a cure. A player at 0% health now always dies: the death screen comes back the moment anything takes it away.

**Respawning after a dungeon death no longer drops you from the sky.** While the town outside was still loading, your character could fall from the dungeon's height onto a roof and take the fall's damage - sometimes enough to die again. You now wait in place until the ground is there, then stand on it. The same goes for Recall, fast travel, a quest's teleport and loading a save.
Fixes and improvements.
Fixes and improvements.

**Your crew have names.** Every hand you see on deck has a name and a job: your First Mate, your Bard, a Bosun, a Gunner, a Carpenter and more. They remember the fights and boardings they've been through. When one falls in battle you'll hear who, and new hires sign on with names of their own. Your own crew's lines show their name.

**Your crew have names.** Every hand you see on deck has a name and a job: your First Mate, your Bard, a Bosun, a Gunner, a Carpenter and more. They remember the fights and boardings they've been through. When one falls in battle you'll hear who, and new hires sign on with names of their own. Your own crew's lines show their name.

**Crew spirits.** Your crew's spirits rise with victories, prizes, plunder, time in port and a round of grog, and sink with losses, a wreck and long voyages away from port. High spirits mean a faster reload, quicker mending and an extra hand in a boarding; low spirits slow them down, darken their chatter and stop the singing. No wages, and nobody deserts.

**Crew spirits.** Your crew's spirits rise with victories, prizes, plunder, time in port and a round of grog, and sink with losses, a wreck and long voyages away from port. High spirits mean a faster reload, quicker mending and an extra hand in a boarding; low spirits slow them down, darken their chatter and stop the singing. No wages, and nobody deserts.

**Give orders.** Use the **Orders** button on the helm panel, or **Give orders** in your boat's menu: **Man the guns** (faster reload), **All hands to the rail** (the crew musters to repel boarders, one more hand in the fight), **Make repairs**, or **Stand down**. Your First Mate answers by name. **Crew** in the boat menu shows everyone aboard and how their spirits stand.

**Give orders.** Use the **Orders** button on the helm panel, or **Give orders** in your boat's menu: **Man the guns** (faster reload), **All hands to the rail** (the crew musters to repel boarders, one more hand in the fight), **Make repairs**, or **Stand down**. Your First Mate answers by name. **Crew** in the boat menu shows everyone aboard and how their spirits stand.

**Give orders.** Use the **Orders** button on the helm panel, or **Give orders** in your boat's menu: **Man the guns** (faster reload), **All hands to the rail** (the crew musters to repel boarders, one more hand in the fight), **Make repairs**, or **Stand down**. Your First Mate answers by name. **Crew** in the boat menu shows everyone aboard and how their spirits stand.

**Repair at sea.** Buy **Carpenter's Stores** at the shipwright (they sit in your hold). At sea, order **Make repairs** and, with no enemy near, your crew mends the hull and sails all the way to full, and can refloat a wreck. Each store covers a tenth of the ship; when you run out, or she's whole, your First Mate tells you. The free patch-up to half strength still works as before.

**Repair at sea.** Buy **Carpenter's Stores** at the shipwright (they sit in your hold). At sea, order **Make repairs** and, with no enemy near, your crew mends the hull and sails all the way to full, and can refloat a wreck. Each store covers a tenth of the ship; when you run out, or she's whole, your First Mate tells you. The free patch-up to half strength still works as before.

**An outage no longer costs your online progress.** Your online character saves to the server every two minutes, and when you leave. If the server could not be reached, that save used to live only in the open game page. Closing, reloading or leaving to the menu before the server came back lost everything since the last save it took. Every online save is now also kept on your device until the server takes it. The next time you play that character, you carry on from it, and the game tells you so.

**Closing the game no longer loses your last minutes.** When you closed the page, the game sometimes gave up your character before its final save reached the server, and that save was refused. The kept copy now covers this too.
A kept save is only used if nothing newer reached the server since, from another device, a trade or a purchase. Otherwise the server's save is played and the kept copy is discarded.
**Long-lived characters are covered too.** A very large save is packed small before it is kept on your device, so it fits where the full save would not.

**Running out of fatigue in the water no longer kills you on the spot.** It used to, whatever your health. Now you lose a tenth of your health every few seconds while you stay in the water with no fatigue left, and the screen says **"You are too exhausted to swim - get out of the water!"** From full health that's about 50 seconds to reach the shore, where you collapse and rest as you would anywhere on land.

**Fishing stops before you're worn out.** In a lake you fish while swimming, and treading water tires you as swimming does. Once you are down to the last quarter of your fatigue, the net won't cast in the water, and a cast already out ends. The prompt says **"too tired to fish in the water - get out and rest"**. On a pier or a boat's deck nothing changes: fish as long as you like.

**Your gathering tools work from the hotbar.** Use the Wood-Axe at a tree, the Pick-Axe at an ore vein or a boulder (in the wilderness or a dungeon), the Sickle at an herb patch, the Basket at a patch, or the Fishing-Net in water, from your hotbar or a quick slot, and it does exactly what pressing E there does: the gathering starts, and the goods go to your Stores with the profession's XP. The Sickle always picks the herbs and the Basket always searches for food, whichever one the patch's prompt is showing. With the Sickle, keep still until it's done - you don't need to hold E. The Fishing-Net makes a short cast; hold E instead for a longer one. If the spot needs something first, such as a higher rank, or you've already gathered it today, the tool says so.

**Anywhere else, a tool no longer fills your pack.** Used away from its spot, or from the open pack, the Wood-Axe, Pick-Axe, Sickle, Basket and Fishing-Net no longer make Wood Bundles, fish or other finds, start Foraging's quests or wear down. Instead the tool tells you where its profession is done, for example: *"Logging is done at a tree in the wilderness: walk up to one until the prompt shows, then press E (or use the Wood-Axe)."* Offline, and for guests without the professions, the tools work as they always have. The Spade still robs graves.

**The Professions page explains how to gather** Herbalism, Mining and Logging, as it already did for Hunting and Fishing, including using the tool from your hotbar at the spot. The empty Stores say where their goods come from.

**The bank window names the region whose account it shows** ("Account in Wayrest"), and lists the gold you've banked in other regions beneath it. Every bank online is the Bank of the Empire, but each region still keeps its own account: gold deposited in Daggerfall is in Daggerfall's account.

**Fixed the overworld frame rate sinking over time.** An enemy from a camp you had left behind could be restored by a load over ground that wasn't there yet, and fall forever, each second of the fall costing more. Enemies over ground that hasn't loaded now wait for it, then stand on it.
**A townsperson who knows where a quest's own building is always marks it on your map** when you ask them outdoors (it used to be about one answer in four; the rest said "north of here").
**A house a townsperson marked for a quest is ringed on the town map.** On the Enhanced town map it looked like any other house.

**Houses' doors say "Residence"** and list **Go in** and **Buy it** when you point at them, and a click goes in. Clicking any house used to ask "This house can be your home ... Buy it?". The quest's house reads by its own name, "The <name> Residence", and is never for sale.

**Houses' doors say "Residence"** and list **Go in** and **Buy it** when you point at them, and a click goes in. Clicking any house used to ask "This house can be your home ... Buy it?". The quest's house reads by its own name, "The <name> Residence", and is never for sale.

**No more light-blue rectangles on the sea in the Overworld view.** The surf along the coast was drawn from high above, where it showed as flat sheets over the water. It now shows only at ground level, as it should.

**Your bank account is the same at every bank.** Online, the Bank of the Empire now keeps one account for you. Gold and letters of credit paid in at any bank can be drawn at any other. Before, each region kept its own account, so money deposited in one region was missing from every other region's bank.

**Nothing to do on your side.** The next time you play an online character, the gold in all your regional accounts is moved into the one account, and the game tells you how much came in. No gold is lost or added.
Houses, ships, guild deposits, the market, homes, decor, rent and the Marks all pay from and into the one account.
A loan still belongs to the region where you took it. Its due date, its default and the reputation a default costs stay in that region. The account pays it back.
**The Empire tells you when it takes your gold for a default.** If a loan goes into default, the Empire pays it from your account, and now says how much it took. Before, the gold left without a word.
**When the Warden falls, a damage chart ranks everyone in the fight** by the damage they dealt. It shows on the right side of the screen for a minute and fades out.

**Each row shows** your rank, name and level, a bar of your damage next to the top fighter's, the number, your share of the court's total, the hits you landed on him and your biggest one, the damage you put into the Crystals of Oblivion, and how many times you fell.
**Your own row is outlined and marked "(you)".** In a big court the top ten are listed, and if you're further down your own row shows underneath at your rank, with the rest counted.
The numbers come from the server's own count of the fight, the same count that decides who earns a receipt.
**The Warden's Marks card no longer covers the middle of the screen** when you step into the court. It sits low on the right, clear of your crosshair, and still fades after a few seconds.

**The phase name is gone from under his health bar.** The marks on the bar still show where each phase turns, and each turn is still announced when it happens. The fighter count, the Reckoning countdown and Dagon's Wrath countdown stay.

**Walking over a piece of loot no longer picks it up.** Look at a piece and press activate to take it, like any loot pile, so crossing the court for the piece you want doesn't sweep up the rest. Anything you leave on the floor still goes into your pack when you leave the court.

**A quest monster killed by a party member now counts for your quest, wherever you are.** When you share a quest with your party and then die or leave while its monster is still standing, the monster passes to the party member nearest it. If that member hadn't taken the quest themselves and killed the monster with nobody on the quest nearby, the kill counted for nobody, and the monster was back when you returned. Now the kill reaches your quest, and the quest of every party member who shares it, as it happens.

**Your quest's monsters are yours.** Players outside your party can't see them, hit them or be attacked by them, so someone else clearing a dungeon never takes your quest's target. A dungeon's own monsters, a cave's tigers included, are everyone's, and come back an hour after they die.

**Resting gives magicka back up to half your pool.** Resting, collapsing from exhaustion, and arriving from a cautious journey all refill magicka to 50% of your maximum and no further. "Rest until healed" stops there. If you're already above half, for example after a potion, resting never takes any back.

**Restore Power potions top up the rest.** Each potion restores 5 magicka plus 4 per level. It now costs what it restores at your level, 1 gold per point of magicka, before haggling: about 9 gold at level 1, 45 at level 10 and 85 at level 20.
**Every alchemist sells them.** Each alchemist has 20 Restore Power potions on the shelf every day.

**The Mages Guild sells them to anyone.** Use the guild's magic-items merchant. Members of rank 3 and up see the potions next to the usual magic items. Everyone else, members or not, can buy the potions there instead of being turned away.
Selling a Restore Power potion back is priced the same way, so buying potions to resell never pays.

**Sell anything from your pack.** Under **My listings**, choose **A piece from your pack (gold)** and set a price in gold. The piece leaves your pack at once. If you cancel, or it doesn't sell within 72 hours, it comes back. The new **Goods** view lists everyone's pieces.
A piece bought at a board in its seller's region reaches your pack at once. From another region it comes by courier.
bound pieces (Sigil Stones and the Sigil Broker's wares)
anything you're wearing, locked pieces, quest items and summoned items
gold, letters of credit, boat deeds and boat parts
arrows
Pieces from your pack sell for gold only, not Drakes.
A crafted piece someone else made can't be sold as a crafted piece; only its maker can do that. It sells from your pack, for gold.
**Fixed:** listing a crafted piece someone had traded you made it vanish from your pack. It now stays.

**Yard pieces stay off the road.** A piece could be set down on the street, on its edges or on a track running past town, and the blue lot edge ran across the road. A piece on the road is now refused with a message, and the lot edge runs along the side of the road. Pieces can still touch the road's edge.
**No more furniture through your walls outside.** A long piece turned at an angle could be placed cutting through the corner of your house. It's now refused until it's clear of the wall.
**Yard changes stick.** A piece you had just placed could vanish, or one you had removed could come back, for about a minute. Your changes now stay put.
**Yards don't blink at map edges.** Walking across a map boundary near decorated yards made their pieces disappear for a moment. They now stay in place.

**You can paint your house's outside again.** In the Decorate panel's Exterior tab, the "Paint it", "Put back" and "The town's own" buttons were hidden. A look you tried disappeared as soon as you left the tab. Press "Paint it" to keep a look for everyone.
A look you just painted no longer flips back to the old one for up to a minute. That could happen when the town's list of homes refreshed at the same moment, or when you painted twice in a row.
Closing the decorator after trying a look you didn't paint now reopens the Exterior tab on your house's real look, not on the one you put away.
**Tenants can rest.** If you rent a room in someone's home, you can now rest there. Before, it said "You have not rented a room here."

**Renewing only offers the days you can buy.** A room can be paid at most 30 days ahead. When you renew, the door now lists only the day counts that fit, and tells you when your room is already paid that far. Before, it offered 30 days anyway, refused the rent, and moved the cost from your purse to the bank.
**Rent paid while you're home shows up.** The "Rooms to rent" tab checks again each time you open the Decorate panel, and every half minute while it's open.

**Offers in a house that is one room again stay listed.** You can still see your tenants and stop offering a room. Before, visitors could rent a room you could no longer see. While your rooms are still being found, the tab says "Finding the rooms of your house..." instead of "A house of one room...".
**Room numbers match.** A room you offer as "Room 2" is "Room 2" at the door, not "Room 1".
**The door opens right after you rent.** Before, it could stay locked for up to a minute.
If the owner stops offering your room, the door now says your room can't be renewed and how many days you have left.

**Running keeps every step past 100.** A mastered skill past 100 stopped counting after about an hour and a half of running between rests, and the extra progress from a long run was thrown away. Now all of it counts, and whatever a rest doesn't turn into a point is kept for the next rest.

**Climbing past 100 does something now.** Climbing is already a sure thing at 95, so a mastered Climbing gained nothing past 100. Now each point past 100 makes you climb faster: about 8% faster at 125, 17% at 150 and 40% at 200.
**The change to magic is undone.** The last update made resting refill magicka only to half your pool, and changed how Restore Power potions are sold and priced. That's reverted.
**Restore Power potions are back to their old price and shops.** Alchemists and the Mages Guild no longer carry them; temples and the Dark Brotherhood sell potions to their members as before.

**Rain no longer vanishes when you sink into a puddle.** Standing in a puddle or other shallow water hid the rain and the sand while you could still hear it. Now the falling weather is only hidden when your eyes are actually under the water.

**Rain isn't always a downpour any more.** A rainstorm now drizzles at its edges and only pours at its heart, so a light sprinkle or a gentle shower is common, and snow falls lightly more often. A light rain also looks light, with thinner fog and more daylight. The dark, foggy look comes in with the heavy rain.

**Rain isn't always a downpour any more.** A rainstorm now drizzles at its edges and only pours at its heart, so a light sprinkle or a gentle shower is common, and snow falls lightly more often. A light rain also looks light, with thinner fog and more daylight. The dark, foggy look comes in with the heavy rain.
**Distant clouds no longer look square.** Far-off clouds near the horizon could show blocky, square edges, worst on the lower cloud quality setting. They're smooth now.

**The sea looks like water from underneath.** Underwater is murkier now: the water is a blue-green that swallows reds first, gets darker the deeper you dive and at night, and closes off the distance sooner.

**Sunbeams shine down through the water.** On a sunny day, shafts of light reach down from the surface. They lean with the sun, shift as the waves pass, and fade as you go deeper, under clouds and at night.
**Weather fills the Overworld view.** Rain, snow, sand and wind used to show only as a small patch around your character. Now they fill the air in front of the camera, as they do on the ground.

**Your character faces the way you're going.** In the Overworld, the movement keys turn your character toward the direction you press, so you see them walk off to the side or come toward the camera instead of always seeing their back.

**Other players show up in the Overworld.** Other players were drawn at normal size from high up, so all you could see was their name over a tiny speck. They're now drawn as large as your own character, whether they're on foot, riding or in a Morrowind body.

**Smoother turning in a crowd with the Morrowind model.** Turning to face a group of players could stall a frame while every body that came into view was posed at once. Bodies about to come into view are now prepared a little ahead of the turn, a few at a time.

**Fewer rebuilds of other players' Morrowind bodies.** Another player drawing a different weapon, mounting a horse or stepping out of sight for a moment no longer makes their whole body load again; the weapon simply changes in their hand.

**No more stalls along the coast.** Walking or sailing along a coastline could stall the game for a moment each time you crossed into a new area, while the surf along the shore was rebuilt. The rebuild now takes a few milliseconds instead.

**Ships in the distance cost less.** The small details on far-off ships, such as lanterns, are no longer drawn once they're smaller than a pixel, just like the ships' own fittings, and ships' flags take less work to draw every frame.

Climbing now knows what a ledge is. Face a ledge and press **Jump**, and you pull yourself up onto it instead of jumping.

**Forward**, or a fresh press of **Jump**, climbs up onto the top, or over it if it's thin. A ledge with no room above it, such as a window sill, just keeps you hanging.

**Corners:** the shimmy goes round the corners of a building, inside and out, and round towers and rooms of any shape: square, eight-sided or round. Keep the key held and you carry on round. Going round a corner uses your grip like the rest of the shimmy.
**Back** climbs down the wall under you.
**Crouch** lets go. You fall from where you were hanging, so the drop is shorter than it looks from the top.
Hold **Forward** against a wall for a moment and you climb it. There's no dice roll any more and no random slipping.
**Forward** climbs up, **Back** climbs down, **Left** and **Right** move across. Let go of the keys and you stay where you are.
**Jump with Forward held** at a sheer wall grabs it straight from the jump.

Save while you hang or climb and the load puts you back on the wall where you were, with the grip you had left. Save in the middle of a climb onto a ledge and you load at the end of it.
Carrying more than half of what you can carry shortens your reach. With a full pack, a ledge has to be about 30 cm lower to reach.
**Climbing** sets how high you can reach, how fast you pull yourself up, climb and shimmy, how long your grip lasts, and how long a fall you can still catch.
Past 100, Climbing still makes you climb and shimmy faster, up to 1.4 times as fast at 200, just as it does for ordinary climbing.

Climbing onto or over something, and catching a ledge or a wall, each cost about as much fatigue as a jump and train **Climbing**. A vault trains **Jumping**. Time on a wall costs fatigue as climbing always has, and trains Climbing as often as the old climb did.

**The view moves with you.** A catch jolts the view down, harder after a long fall. Hanging sways a little. Shimmying and climbing rock from one hand to the other. Fixes and improvements.

**Gear wears at about Daggerfall's own rate.** Two of the combat mods made weapons wear several times faster than the original game, and armour many times faster. Their wear options are now off by default, online and offline.

**Only the damage that gets through wears your gear.** Under the combat overhaul, armour soaks up part of a blow instead of turning it aside, so a blow wears your weapon and the piece it hits by what got past the armour. Good armour wears slower.
**Claws and bites no longer wear your armour.** Only blows from weapons do, as in the original game.
**Broken enchanted gear is no longer destroyed.** It breaks and stays in your pack, and a smith can repair it.

**Repairs cost half as much.** Every smith and guild now charges a third of Daggerfall's repair price, down from two thirds. With the slower wear, keeping a Daedric longsword in shape costs between a seventh and a tenth of what it did, and Daedric armour far less.

**Repair kits mend up to three quarters.** Field Repair Kits and smith-made Repair Kits now restore a piece to about three quarters of its condition at most. That keeps your gear working in the field; a smith restores it fully, and a freshly sharpened blade hits harder than a worn one.

**A kit isn't wasted.** If everything it could mend is already at three quarters or more, it tells you so and isn't used up, from your pack or from the hotbar. It won't spend itself on a piece that's only a sliver below three quarters.

**A kit asks before it goes on the wrong piece.** If your worn gear is past three quarters and the only piece the kit can mend is something else you're carrying, it asks first, and you can keep the kit.

**Shops pay for worn loot as you found it.** A weapon or piece of armour you loot, or buy worn from a shop, sells for no more than the condition it was in when you got it, even after a repair. Repairs are for using your gear, not for selling it. Gear that came to you whole sells at its own condition, as before. Offline, nothing changes.
**Alchemists always stock Potions of Healing.** Every alchemist has a few each day (more in a better shop), and general stores keep one to three. Online they're half price, like every potion.
**You'll find more of them.** Enemies that carry loot sometimes have one, and the treasure piles in most dungeons hold one more often than before.

**Your crew companions carry what a person of their strength can.** A companion's pack now has a weight limit based on their strength: from about 67 kg to about 97 kg, depending on their class. A strength spell you cast on them raises it. The pack window shows how much they're carrying.
When a pack is full, the companion says they can't carry any more. If you store gold, they take only what they can carry.

Offline, you can turn the combat overhaul's own wear back on, on Physical Combat And Armor Overhaul's tile on the Features page. It wears gear the way that mod does, a little faster than the old default. If you had changed these options before, they've been reset once.

**Herb patches, ore veins, boulders, trees, bodies and fishing water now use the loot list.** Look at one and the same box that lists a body's loot shows its name, your profession, and what you can do there: "Pick Red Rose", "Quarry the stone", "Skin the Grizzly Bear", "Search the Grizzly Bear", and so on.
**Pick an action the way you take loot.** Click it, press your activate key, or tap it. The Up arrow moves to the next action; you can rebind it in Controls.
**An action you can't do yet says why**, right on its row: no tool, rank too low, or the day's limit reached.
Starting a hold action (kneeling, steadying, skinning) from the list holds it for you, the same as using the tool from the hotbar.
On the Classic skin and on touch screens, where the loot box isn't shown, the same choices come up as a small list window.
The gathering minigames no longer open a panel over the screen. Each one is drawn on and around your crosshair, so you can see the world while you work. The rules and timings haven't changed.

**Logging:** a ring closes on the notch around your crosshair. It lights up in the band where a strike is a Clean Cut.
**Herbs:** your hold fills as an arc around the crosshair. It turns orange if you bruise the plant by moving.

Works for every quick-loot take, one item or Take All, from a body, a dropped pile or a catch of fish.

**The bushes around bandit camps and other World of Daggerfall sites no longer float in the air or sink into the hillside.** Each one now stands on the ground under it. Tents, fires, walls and rocks are where they were.

**The leader keeps the Party tab while the party readies up.** Choosing a destination on the travel map used to close the Party tab, taking the ready count and Call off with it. It now comes back when the map closes.

**Every blow wears your weapon and armour twice as much as before.** A steel longsword now loses about an eighth of its condition over a hundred swings (it was about a sixteenth). Armour wears faster too, though good armour still lasts.
**Still far gentler than before the last update.** Armour wears a fraction of what it did then, and a monster's claws still don't wear it at all.

**More boulders, and at the rock.** A rock field's boulders mostly never appeared, and the few that did often had their loose stones out on open ground, well away from any rock. **Twice as many nodes.** Every map square now holds twice the herb patches, trees and ore veins each day, in every climate (woodlands: 8 herb patches, 12 trees, 4 veins). The daily limit per profession is unchanged, so you gather the same amount in a day, with less walking between nodes.

Only the nearest twelve within about 3 km are shown, and a group you've worked out disappears.
**Gathering filter.** The Overworld's filters have a new **Gathering** switch to hide or show them.
Clicking a group walks you to that spot, as clicking open ground does.
Players standing close together on screen show as one larger dot, such as "5 travellers".
Players off the edge of your screen in roughly the same direction share one arrow.
Only the six players nearest you on screen show their full title, Renown, guild tag and glyphs; others, and players off the edge of the screen, show just their name.
Your party is always shown in full.

**One friend list on every device.** Your friends, requests and party were tied to the browser you played in, so a laptop and a desktop each had their own list. They now belong to your account: the same list wherever you sign in. The first time each of your devices connects after this update, the friends it knew are added to your list, so nobody is lost.
**A friend list can't be taken over.** A friend list that someone else had set up under your account before this update is thrown away, not given to you.
**An old copy of the game says so.** If a tab or the desktop app is still running an older build, it now tells you to update the game to see your friends and party, instead of showing an empty list.

**Cast when used items work in dungeons.** A bracer of Ice Storm, a scarab of Fireball, or any item that casts a spell when used now casts it underground. Before, the click just swung your weapon, the item still lost condition, and the spell went off the next time you clicked outside.

**A spell readied from an item goes through doors with you.** Use an item, then step into or out of a dungeon, and the spell is still ready to cast. It no longer fires by itself once you're back outside, or vanishes.
**The right cost underground.** The readied-spell line in a dungeon showed an item's spell at its full spell-point cost. An item's spell costs you nothing, and now it says so.
**Slowfall no longer sticks you to walls.** A slow fall that drifted into a wall could catch onto it, or hang on a steep cliff face, before you reached the ground. Now you slide down and land.
**No more hard landing after a slow fall.** Slipping off a wall you were climbing while Slowfall was on used to drop you at full speed and hurt. Now you come down gently.
**Steep slopes while Jump is active.** With the Jump spell's air control, holding Forward into a steep face no longer holds you up on it.
**Gliding onto a roof.** A slow glide that reaches a lower roof's edge still steps up onto it.

**Turn and tilt the 3D map together.** Holding the right mouse button now turns and tilts the dungeon map at the same time. A small wobble while you turn still doesn't tilt it, but a real move up or down does, for the rest of that drag.

**World of Daggerfall's mountains look like rock.** The big rock formations and mountains had their texture stretched across hundreds of metres, so they looked like smeared ground reaching into the sky. Their rock now repeats at a natural scale, so it shows as rock from up close to about a kilometre away. Their size and shape haven't changed.
**Planks and stone stay straight.** Fort palisades and dock stonework keep their planks and blocks running the right way.

**The game's cursor stays the game's cursor.** Hovering over a menu's scrollbar, or moving close to the right or bottom edge of the screen, no longer swaps the custom cursor for your system's arrow. This works with both the classic and the enhanced look.
**Tidier scrollbars.** Menu scrollbars use the game's slim stone style. On a phone or tablet, scrollbars stay hidden as before.

**Area spells of buffs reach you.** An Area at Range or Area Around Caster spell made only of buffs, such as Regenerate with Fortify, also lands on you when you cast it. This came in the previous update.

**A day online is now 30 minutes.** Nights, full moons and quest hours come round four times as often. Midnight falls on the hour and the half hour, real time, and dusk at :22:30 and :52:30 (the Online page gives your own clock's times).

A vampire waits at most 15 real minutes for nightfall, and the message counts it right.
The world's business keeps its pace: shops, prices, guild shelves, weather fronts, gates and raids. The weather follows the sky's season and time of day.
Gate and raid messages now give your local time only.
Online, the full moon forces the change for its night only, from dusk to dawn: 15 real minutes. At dawn you can change back.
Full-moon nights come two real hours apart, then none for fourteen.
Quest timers now run on your own clock. Resting, waiting and travel spend them, as in Daggerfall: "come back in 3 days" is a 72-hour rest, about half a minute.
Time away is still never charged. A closed or hidden tab costs a quest timer half an hour of game time at most.
A quest's hours ("daily from 12:00 to 13:00"), the date and the season follow the sky. A daily window comes round every 30 real minutes.
Journal dates match the calendar you see.
In a party, each member's copy of a shared quest runs on that member's clock. When a timer runs out on one copy, it runs out for the whole party.
Quest timers ran a fifth to a third slow while you played, offline too. They count every second now.
Online saves made before this update move their quest timers onto your clock the first time they load. Older saves otherwise load as before.
Fixes and improvements.

**No more giant dark shards hanging in the sky.** The last update's fix for floating bushes around bandit camps also lifted the big boulders that World of Daggerfall's rock fields are built from. They stuck up out of their rock piles as huge dark slabs, some hundreds of metres tall, around Hadus and near rock fields everywhere. The boulders are back where the mod sets them, down in the rock.

**Tall dungeon walls can be climbed again.** Dungeon walls are built from stacked sections. Where the section above sticks out a little, such as the edge of a doorway or a pillar, your climb used to stop about 1.4 m up, under it. That's how a "two blocks" wall left you stuck in a pit. Now you shift along the wall past it, up to about half a metre, and keep climbing.
**Low Climbing skill gets you off the ground.** Some large dungeon walls stopped a climber with low Climbing skill right at the floor. You now climb them at your normal pace.

**No more falling off at gaps in a wall.** Some dungeon walls have a thin gap between two sections. The climb used to treat the gap as a ledge, grab it, then let go and drop you to the floor, again and again. It now climbs straight past it.

**Climbing past a step in a wall.** Where the upper part of a wall sits a little further back than the lower part, you used to stop at the step, or grab it and fall off. Now you climb past it and carry on to the top. Climbing back down, you stop on the wall above the step, as you do above a window sill.

**Climbing in a corner.** In a narrow shaft you can end up on the side wall instead of the one you're facing. When the wall you're turned towards has a top within reach, you now climb onto it, instead of carrying on up the side wall.
**Climbing down from just over a step or a recess** in a wall no longer freezes you or makes you let go. You climb down to the floor.
**No more letting go near a sloping top.** Where a wall's top leans back at a corner, you could let go and fall from high up. You now hold on.
**Turning your view while you climb** no longer pulls you sideways onto a crate, a low wall or a fence beside the wall.

**Enemies near you end a hunt.** When you're offered a hunt on the road ("You spot a set of animal tracks..."), an enemy that comes near (or a duel opponent) now closes the offer, or ends the search if you've already started, so you can turn and fight. Nothing is searched and no time passes. The result page itself stays until you close it, so close it quickly if an enemy is coming.

**No ambush while you read the result.** The time a hunt takes now passes when you close the result, not while it's on screen. Before, a wandering enemy could appear and walk up while you were still reading.
A hunt is no longer offered while an enemy nearby is still on its way in.
**Loading a save with a hunt open** no longer charges the loaded game the hunt's time or puts its animal there.

**No fishing prompt at the helm.** At sea, the "Open Water / Cast the net" prompt sat in the middle of the screen while you steered, and got in the way when you aimed the bow guns. It no longer appears while you're at the helm, aiming the guns or boarding. You can still fish from a deck you're standing on.

**The ship's sound no longer cuts out.** Taking the helm and getting under way, or slowing down, used to restart the boat's sound from the beginning, so it cut out. The sound now carries on smoothly as you speed up and slow down.
**No more silent boats.** With more than one boat nearby, one could be left silent until it started moving. Every boat can be heard now.

The enhanced pack's paperdoll card now has a **Stats** button at the bottom centre of the card, in the figure's own column (it no longer sits on the right weapon's slot). Pressing it turns the card over on a 3D hinge (lift, shadow, content rising in) to a combat page; the button then reads **Paperdoll** and turns it back.
**Damage** (min-max and average), **hit chance**, **critical chance** and what a critical does, **backstab chance**, and the expected damage of an average swing.
A table per **swing direction** (sideways, thrust, down-right, down-left, overhead; a bow shows its release).
**Breakdown**: weapon roll, material, Strength, proficiency, race, your attack term, the foe's armour and dodging.
**Defence** (overall armour, the seven part numbers, dodging, biography, health), **attributes** with their effects, and the skills in play.

The hit and damage are scored against a foe of your level in four real armour classes (chips at the top): **Soft / Tough / Armoured monster** (armour value 6 / 0 / -10, as the bestiary stores them) and a **Human foe** in mail.
Enhanced skin only; the classic canvas window is untouched.
`prefers-reduced-motion` gets a crossfade instead of the turn.
The page wears the window's pixel face (`PIXEL_STACK`: Pixelify Sans, Silkscreen's 5), not Barlow / Cormorant.
**The shimmer is gone**: the light sweep across the card while it turns is removed (the turn, lift, shadow and rising content stay).

**The hit chances were far too high.** The old reference foes were a hybrid: a class (human) foe's armour numbers (100 = unarmoured) with a monster's +40 (overhaul +50) bonus to be hit, so a bare foe read 97% whatever your skill. They are now the real thing: monsters carry `armorValue x 5` (the bestiary runs -12..7, so 30 / 0 / -50 on each part) with the monster bonus; the human is a class foe with no bonus, and the overhaul reads the flat 60 it reads off every class foe (`pcaaoArmorToHit`). Damage figures were right and are unchanged.

**Grass is no longer dark.** Up close, tufts of grass used to look almost black against the ground they grew from, and darker still at dusk, in rain and in storms. Grass is now painted in the ground's own colours: the base of each tuft matches the ground under it, and the blades get lighter towards their sunlit tips.

**Grass blends into the land.** Grass takes its colour from whatever ground it grows on, so it matches in every climate and season: the lush green of the woodlands, the grey-green of the mountains, the deep green of the swamps.
**No more yellow band.** The grass a little way off used to show as a yellowish stripe across the field. Now the far grass fades into the ground's own colour.
**Grass is lit like the ground.** At dawn, at dusk, under clouds and by moonlight, the grass now takes exactly the same light as the ground under it, with Enhanced lighting on or off.
**Shade falls on the grass.** Grass in the shade of a tree, a wall or a passing cloud is now shaded like the ground around it, instead of staying in full sun.
**Rain doesn't darken the grass twice.** Grass used to be darkened for bad weather on top of the dimmer light the weather already brings. Now it's darkened once, like everything else.
**Lanterns and torches light the grass.** At night, grass near a lantern, a campfire or the torch in your hand now glows along with the ground under it, instead of staying dark beside the lit ground.
**Grass on hillsides.** Grass on a slope facing away from the sun is now shaded like the slope, instead of staying as bright as grass on level ground.
**Texture mods.** With a texture mod that replaces the ground, grass now takes its colours from the mod's ground.
**Classic lighting.** With Enhanced lighting off, grass is no longer brighter and greener than it is with Enhanced lighting on.
The grass is under *Sight* in Features: **Grass** sets how much grass grows and its style (Pixel or Smooth). Both styles get the new colours and light.

**Trees grow together in forests.** Trees used to be spread evenly over the whole map, one every few steps, all lined up in rows. Now they gather into woods, from small copses to forests a few kilometres across, with open grassland between them dotted with bushes, flowers, rocks and the odd lone tree.
**Forests run on from one area to the next.** A forest doesn't stop where the land around you finishes loading.
**No more rows.** Every tree and bush stands at its own spot, so a wood looks like a wood.

**Dungeons hide in the woods.** Dungeons, ruins, shrines, graveyards, covens and World of Daggerfall's camps, forts and ruins are usually surrounded by forest, with a clearing round them big enough for their tents and walls. Towns, farms and taverns stand in cleared fields. World of Daggerfall's rock fields and mountains are scenery: the woods grow round them as anywhere else, but never through the rocks.
**Paths stay clear.** No tree or bush grows on a road or a track.
**The Oblivion Gate keeps its clearing.** No tree stands through the gate, its plinth or the Sigil Broker.
**Deserts are unchanged.** The Desert and Subtropical lands keep Daggerfall's own scattered plants.
**Loggers chop in the woods.** The day's trees to fell stand in the forests whenever there's a forest nearby. The lone trees of open land are only used where there's no wood at all.
**Real forests** is under *The world* in Features. It's on by default and takes effect when the world next loads. Turn it off to spread the trees evenly, as Daggerfall does.

Forests hold more trees than Daggerfall's even scatter, about two and a half times as many on average. If the outdoors runs slowly on your machine, turning Real forests off is one more way to lighten it.
