**Three Motherlodes break ground every day**, each in its own part of the day, on ground players have explored. Each stands for **two hours**, or until **20 miners** have struck it.

**You are warned in the chat 10 minutes before one rises**, with its region and its ore. With the **Motherlode Sense** specialisation (Mining 100), the warning comes 30 minutes ahead. Motherlode Sense can now be chosen.

**Find it on your compass** from anywhere in the open world, in Mining's colour. Close up it is a large, glowing heap of ore at a rock (where a town covers the middle of its ground, it stands at the nearest open spot outside the town).

**Strike it with your Pick-Axe** like a vein, at its tier-6 difficulty. It needs **Mining 25**. The Watch must have seen you on its ground in the last few minutes - it marks those who move about, every two minutes. If it hasn't, you are told to walk about on it a moment.
If its twenty miners have struck it, or it has gone, your first try tells you and the Motherlode is gone from your world - no more wasted swings.

**Each strike gives 4 to 6 of its ore** (Adamantium, Ebony or Orichalcum - half again for a clean strike), Mining XP and **10 silver**. Each account can strike **one Motherlode a day**. It does not count against your 60 harvests.

**Each strike gives 4 to 6 of its ore** (Adamantium, Ebony or Orichalcum - half again for a clean strike), Mining XP and **10 silver**. Each account can strike **one Motherlode a day**. It does not count against your 60 harvests.
Renown stays separate from silver: it still raises your health and magicka, opens sigil stages, founds guilds and counts toward a seat's influence.
Fixes and improvements.

**The HUD, your weapon and your horse now stay inside the picture.** With Retro Picture Mode on and Retro Aspect set to 4:3 or 16:10, only the world used to be framed by the black bars. The health bars sat in the left bar, the compass and your weapon hugged the screen's right edge, and the docked large HUD stretched across the whole screen. Now the HUD, the large HUD, your weapon (and the Weapon and Shield Widget sprites), the spellcasting hands and the horse all sit inside the picture, as in Daggerfall Unity. The docked large HUD is the picture's width, so the view above it keeps Daggerfall Unity's shape. On the Enhanced Plus UI, the HUD, notifications, quest tracker and status line stay inside the bars too.

**Notifications you've moved now fade in where you put them.** If you dragged the notifications to a new spot (Alt+U), each new notification first appeared at its old place on the right and then jumped. Now it shows up at your spot from the first frame, and fades in and out there instead of sliding in from the side. Notifications you haven't moved still slide in from the right as before. Revenant taunt cards you've moved fade the same way.

**The classic UI now uses Daggerfall Unity's classic blue arrow cursor.** It shows from the very first screen, over every window and panel, and the gamepad cursor uses the same arrow. Text boxes still show the text cursor. Enhanced Plus keeps its gauntlet.

**Fixed a GPU memory leak in long sessions.** Each time you opened the map inside a dungeon or a building, the game created a new graphics context of 30 to 40 MB (more on a 4K screen) and never freed it. The map now reuses one. The game also releases all its graphics memory as soon as you close the tab, instead of waiting for the browser to get round to it. This mattered most on Firefox.

**Bounty packs no longer spawn inside rocks.** A bounty's pack, a wilderness camp or a roaming band could stand inside one of the World of Daggerfall rock formations or mountains, where you couldn't reach them. They now always stand on open ground.

**The Bodyguard now finishes online once you're paid.** After you saved Evelara from the assassins and were paid, the quest stayed in your journal forever when playing online. It now closes a couple of minutes after the reward, like other finished quests. If it's already stuck in your journal, it closes on its own the next time you play. Offline, it closes the next day, as it always has.

**Inertia now sways the sprites when you look around.** The Inertia module was getting your mouse look in the wrong units, so the sway from turning was about a fourteenth of what the mods intend. Walking and strafing swayed them, but looking around barely did. Turning now sways the weapon, shield and torch as in Daggerfall Unity. Turn the Inertia dials down if it's too much for your taste.

**The Shield Widget's Recoil now kicks when an attack lands on your shield.** With the default armor rules (Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul), the game never told the shield which part of you was hit, so its default "Attack On Shield" recoil never fired. The Weapon Widget's Recoil already worked once its module is switched on.

**Clearer words when the guild treasury can't pay for a hall.** Buying a hall for your guild takes the house's price plus half again, paid from the guild's gold treasury (Social > Guild > Treasury). Only gold that realm characters put into the treasury counts. Gold in a bank account never pays for a hall. The old message ("put in by realm characters") didn't say which of these was the problem, and "realm" read like a place. There are now two separate messages: one when the treasury is short of the price, and one when it holds enough but not enough of that gold counts.
**The Guild tab shows how much of the treasury can buy a hall.**
**Deposit and Withdraw say "at most 1,000,000 at a time"** if you type more than one move allows, instead of failing after you press. A 1,274,880 gold hall takes two deposits.
**A harvest is one card under your crosshair**, in the same place loot cards appear. It shows:
**Gather the same thing again while its card is up** and the card adds to itself (+3, then +5), instead of stacking new lines.
A gem, a Heartwood, a resin or a hide's extra find shows as its own card under the first, with its own Stores count. Fish show their species.
**A Motherlode strike is one bigger card** showing the ore, the 10 silver, your purse and how many of its twenty miners have struck it.
**Silver gets a card wherever you earn it**:
When you have reached the day's combat limit, a muted card says so.
Fixes and improvements.

The **Arena of Daggerfall** now stands in the heart of Daggerfall city, in the block just east of the centre, facing the market. The building is Kamer's **Daggerfall Arena** (used with his permission): high walls, tiers of seats, torches and braziers around a sand floor.
It stands in every game, whether you use Daggerfall's own city layout or Beautiful Cities. It is part of the city, not a switch.
It is drawn with your own copy of Daggerfall's textures, and the stone passages under it are built from your own game's dungeon pieces.
You can walk the tiers and the floor. The walls are solid.

The tavern, the two gem stores and the houses that stood on that block are gone. Every other building in the city keeps its name, its owner and its guild. The Palace, the temple, the guilds and the banks are where they were.
At the north gate you'll find the **Herald of the Arena**, two gate wardens of the Royal Guard, recruiters for the Red Banner and the Blue Banner, and a bookmaker.

Talk to the **Herald** and he gives you a choice: **watch the exhibition**, **fight on the ladder**, open **the Arena window**, **go down to the fighters' hall** (the undercroft), or leave. If a choice isn't open, he tells you why.
The arena's two companies take fighters at the gate. Talk to the **Red Banner Recruiter** or the **Blue Banner Recruiter** to join. Joining is free.
Every ladder bout you win is a point for your banner. Beating a Tier Champion is worth 3, and the Grand Champion 10.
A season lasts a year of the game's calendar. When it ends, the banner with more points wins, and its fighters wear the **laurel** all the next year: the crowd is on your side from the first bell.
You can quit your banner whenever you like (the recruiter asks you twice), but you can't join the other one until the next season. You can go back to the banner you quit at any time.
Each banner fields 24 fighters of its own, who climb the same ladder you do over the season. You'll see them on the leaderboards.
Your banner's pennant shows beside your name on the versus bar. In an exhibition, the Red Banner's fighter faces the Blue Banner's.

**Your colours on the sand:** fight a ladder bout under a banner and the banners around your side of the ring hang in its colour, and your half of the crowd takes on its colour too. At an exhibition, the Red Banner's half of the stands faces the Blue's.
One window for everything at the arena, opened by the Herald, the recruiters and the bookmaker, and once you've joined a banner, from the **Arena** button on the character page of the pause menu.

**Bouts:** the hour's exhibition with both fighters' records and odds (Watch, Wager), and your next ladder bout with its purse (Fight). Watching, wagering and fighting are done at the arena's gate; the window tells you why when you can't.
**Ladder:** the ten tiers, where you stand, every opponent and champion, the purses and the title each tier gives.
**Team:** your banner, the season's standing against the other, the laurel, your points, and your banner's top ten.

**Leaderboards:** the highest tier, the fastest Grand Champion and the banners season by season, with your own row pinned below the top ten. Online, the realm's boards and its Hall of Champions (see **Online** below).

**Records:** your wins, losses, yields, falls, streaks and purses, your last twenty bouts and your wagers. Offline, your last three ladder bouts can be watched again from here (see **Replays** below).
**Rules:** the arena's rules in plain words.
**The Bookmaker** at the gate takes wagers on the hour's exhibition, from 10 to 1000 gold, until the fight begins. One wager a bout.
His odds come from the fighters' records, less the house's tenth. A winning wager pays your stake back plus the odds he gave; a draw gives you your stake back.
He lays no price shorter than 1 to 5: a fighter more likely to win than that is not taken.
If you don't stay to watch, the bout is still fought and your wager is still settled once the hour is over. But leave once the fight has begun and he keeps your stake, whoever was ahead.
He takes no wager on an hour whose bout you have already seen, and the Herald won't stage an hour's exhibition again once its fight has begun.
Collect your winnings at his stall. He pays in person.
The Herald calls you by your arena title when you step onto the sand.

**The Hall of Champions** in the undercroft names every Grand Champion your character has seen: yours first, then each banner fighter who took the title, season by season. Their names hang on a **wall of plaques** beside the Keeper of the Hall. Click a plaque to read whose it is.
Your banner shows on the character sheet beside your arena title and record.

**Exhibitions:** every hour from 8 in the morning to 9 at night, two fighters meet on the arena's sand. Stand near the colosseum and you'll see the bout, hear the crowd and see the fight on your screen. The same hour always brings the same two fighters.

**The Ladder:** ten tiers, from **The Pit** to **The Grand Melee**. Win three bouts in a tier and you face its **Tier Champion**; beat the champion and you climb, and the arena gives you a title. Tier 5's champion is two Warriors at once, Tier 6 throws you to the beasts, Tier 9 is two against one, and Tier 10 is a free-for-all melee before the **Grand Champion**.
Your opponents don't grow with you. The ladder is a fixed mountain.

**Nobody dies on the sand.** At 1 health you go down and the bout is over. Badly hurt (15% health or less)? Sheathe your weapon to yield. Fighters can also be carried out of the ring, and after three minutes the judges decide: damage dealt, then hits landed, then fewer misses.
After every bout the arena's healers make you whole again.
**Purses** run from 50 gold for a first-tier win to 10,000 gold for the Grand Champion. The crowd's favour raises or cuts your purse. Losing costs you only the purse.
While your bout is on, you can't rest, travel or leave through the gates.
Your progress, titles and record are saved with your character. Your arena title and record show on the character sheet.
Strike an exhibition fighter and the Herald will warn you once. Do it again and the watch comes for you.

**Replays:** your last three ladder bouts are kept with your character. Ask the Herald (**R - Watch your last bout again**) or press **Watch the replay** on the Records page, at the arena's gate, and you watch the bout again from the terrace, with the crowd, the Herald and the verdict. A replay pays and counts nothing, and you can leave it whenever you like. (In a replay you appear as a fighter of your class.) Replays are kept offline only: online the realm keeps its own records.
The tiers fill with Daggerfall's own people: the gesturing man, dancers and musicians, courtiers and nobles. Big bouts draw hundreds.

The crowd cheers a great blow, gasps at a telling one, groans at a knockdown and roars at a comeback. It boos stalling, running away and an early yield. A fighter it hates is booed every time they strike.
Each fighter has the crowd's favour, for good or ill. Its darling and its villain are marked on the screen.
The crowd shouts, too: "Blood on the sand!", "Get up, you dog!", and the name of a favourite's home town.
At the verdict the crowd throws flowers for a winner it loves, and something worse for one it doesn't.

The crowd's voices are built while you play from Daggerfall's own crowd recordings. Drums, the bell and the old Arena fanfares are Daggerfall's own sounds. The arena also has its own march and victory fanfare.

A **versus bar** shows both fighters' names and health, your stamina, the crowd's mood and the time left. It takes no keys and never pauses the game. It moves aside for the target frame and the quest card, keeps clear of the crosshair on a short screen, and hides with the rest of the HUD (F10).
The bout's clock stops while the game is paused, so a pause never runs out a bout's time.
The Herald calls each fighter by name, counts down "3 - 2 - 1 - Fight!" and gives the verdict in the middle of the screen.
A stair inside the colosseum leads down to **The Arena Undercroft**: Kamer's own 32-block dungeon under the arena, now the **fighters' hall**.
Nothing down there attacks you, and nothing breaks your rest. You'll find fighters at rest, the arena's keepers, the armourer at his anvil, and the beasts of the beast tier on their chains.
Talk to **the Pit Master** at the training pit to **spar**: a practice bout against a fighter of your own tier. No purse, no crowd, no step on the ladder - just practice.
**The Keeper of the Hall** reads you the **Hall of Champions**: the tier champions you have beaten, and your name as Grand Champion once you earn it.
The **Smaller Dungeons** setting never shrinks the undercroft, so the fighters' hall, the training pit and the Hall of Champions are always where they belong.

**A house:** the Daggerfall Bank moves your deed to a house of the same kind elsewhere in the city, the first time you load. Your own furniture goes back to your furnishings, ready to set down again, and anything you bought from the decorator is paid back in full to your Daggerfall bank account. Everything that was in your chests and on your floor waits for you in a chest in the new house (or in a crate by the door if the house has no chest). You'll get a letter, and a note in your notebook.
**A rented room** at the old tavern is honoured at any inn in the city.
**A quest building** on that block is chosen again in the city, so the quest can still be finished.
**A save made inside one of those buildings**, or a Recall anchor set there, puts you outside instead.
**An online home** on that block moves too (see **Online** below).
Online play needs a relay update (a single reconnect) and a registered account. Guests can watch, but they can't queue, join a banner or keep a result.

**Find a match:** from the Arena window's Bouts page, look for a real opponent at your season rating. Ratings start at 1,000. The search widens every 10 seconds until someone is found. You both have 20 seconds to accept. A fighter who declines isn't offered to you again for a minute.
**Casual bouts:** choose **Casual bout** instead and you're matched only with other players who want one. It's refereed the same way, but nothing is counted: no rating, no points, no record.

**Refereed bouts:** a bout between players is fought on its own copy of the arena floor, and the server referees it. It holds both fighters' health (the same for every fighter of a level) and only counts a blow that could really have landed: in reach, at a believable pace, no harder than your weapon can hit.
Leave a fight for more than 15 seconds and you forfeit it. A matched bout that nobody turns up to is called off.
A win or loss moves your rating. More than five rated bouts in a day against the same fighter are kept, but don't move it.

**The ladder online** is your account's own climb, with opponents the server runs. Wins count only in order, and your purse is paid once the realm has counted the win. Ladder wins (and rated wins against players) also earn **Renown** for the character who fought, within the usual hourly limit.

**The hour's exhibition is the same bout for everyone:** online, the server fights it, so every player at the arena sees the same blows and the same winner. The bookmaker settles your wager by that result.

**The stands:** watch any bout from the Bouts page (exhibitions, players' bouts, ladder bouts; a private session's bouts are watched by joining it), up to 60 watchers a bout. You're seated in the tiers with no body. **Cheer** and **Boo** from the stands (buttons on screen, or the = and - keys), and the whole crowd hears it.

**Banners online** are your account's, not your character's. Seasons last eight weeks. You earn points for your banner: 1 for a ladder win, 3 for a Tier Champion, 10 for the Grand Champion and 2 for a rated win against a player. Last season's winners wear the laurel, and the crowd favours them from the first bell. Every fighter's banner shows on the versus bar.

**Realm leaderboards:** the highest climb, the fastest Grand Champions, the season's player ratings and the banners, with your own row pinned under the top ten. The **Hall of Champions** online names every Grand Champion of the realm, in the window and when the Keeper of the Hall reads it.
**Records online** shows your account's record and your last twenty bouts, with whom you fought and how.

**Titles:** your arena title shows on your letters and notices too. **Grand Champion** is yours for good once the realm has counted all forty ladder wins. The season's #1 player (with at least three rated bouts) wears the title **Arena Champion** and the **laurel** beside their name, until someone else takes the top.

**Host your own session:** open the Arena window (from the Herald, a recruiter or the bookmaker at the arena's gate in Daggerfall, or the pause menu's **Arena** button once you've joined a banner) and, on the Bouts page, press **Host a session** (you need a registered account). You get a six-character code to share on stream or in chat. Codes leave out I, L, O, 0 and 1, so a code read off the screen is typed right, and upper or lower case both work.

**Join one:** type the code into the **Session code** box on the Bouts page and press **Join** (or Enter). You're taken to the arena floor and seated in the stands. Guests can join to watch; fighting needs a registered account. Press Host or Join while outdoors.

**The host decides who fights.** The session's card lists everyone in it. The host presses **Make Red** or **Make Blue** beside a name to pick the two fighters, then **Start bout**: the two are brought down to the sand and everyone else watches from the stands. The host can also **End bout (no result)** while the bout has no result yet, **Remove** someone from the session, **Lock session** so nobody new can join (members who step away can still come back), or **Close session**.

**Every fighter is equal:** in a session's bout both fighters have the same health, whatever their level. The server referees every blow, as in any bout between players, and the Herald calls it a friendly bout. However a bout ends, its fighters are healed and sent back to the stands.
**Nothing is counted:** no rating, no banner points, no records, no Renown. The session keeps its own last 20 results, shown on its card.

A session holds up to 62 people: 60 in the stands and two on the sand. It ends when its host closes it, 15 minutes after the host leaves, or 8 hours after it opened. A host or member who steps out can come back within that time with **Rejoin session** on the card (Host a session always starts a new one).
**The stairs:** every stair in the colosseum now walks smoothly up and down, including the stair from the gate courtyard to the ring. You no longer catch on the steps or start climbing them.

**Paving:** the streets that meet the arena now lead onto paved squares instead of ending in snow, and the gate passage and the courtyard inside the walls are paved too. Lamps, benches, crates and signposts mark the three sides away from the gate.
**The gate's people** are known by what they do: the Herald of the Arena, the Red Banner Recruiter, the Blue Banner Recruiter, the Bookmaker and the Arena Wardens.
**The entrance:** fighters now walk out from the gates under the stands to their marks as the Herald calls their names.
**The judges** now count missed swings (yours and your opponent's), so "fewer misses" can settle a close bout.
**The crowd** gasps at a real critical strike now, not just at any big hit.
**The stands:** the noble lords and ladies in the crowd are their proper size.
**Your character** now faces the way you do when you arrive somewhere (on the sand, through a door), instead of turning to face the camera.
Thin lines of sky that showed through some of the colosseum's walls, and flickering streaks on an inner wall, are gone.
A torch left burning in a house that was moved for the arena now waits for you in the new house's chest.
The colosseum draws faster, and building it for the first time no longer stalls the game.
**Beautiful Villages of Daggerfall** (by carademono) lays out every village, hamlet, farm, manor and temple in the Iliac Bay again, and rebuilds the roadside taverns.
**Beautiful Cities of Daggerfall** (by carademono) lays out all 410 cities again, with districts, walls, gates, markets and docks.

Both are on by default. Each has its own switch in the Features pane (under Mods). A change takes effect the next time the game starts, so a town never changes around you. Offline, the new towns also need Replace Game Artwork switched on.
Roadside taverns keep their inn. A few of the new village blocks have no tavern in them, so those 274 roadside taverns stay as they were in Daggerfall.

Your houses, rented rooms, quest buildings, items left with a smith, Recall anchors set indoors, and saves made inside a building all keep the town layout they were made in. If you switch either mod on or off later, that town keeps its old layout, so your furniture, chests and decorations stay where you left them.

If a town can't be shown in the layout your house was bought in (for example, Replace Game Artwork is switched off), the house isn't treated as yours there, so you never walk into a stranger's home or a shop as its owner. It comes back when the town does.
The first time you load after this update, the game forgets which buildings you had found in towns that changed. The towns themselves stay on your map.
Online, a home can't be bought until the game has loaded the towns as the other players see them. An out-of-date copy of the game is asked to reload before buying.
Online, players who see a town differently are never put in the same building together.
Online, both mods are set for the whole room. Every online home keeps the layout its town had when it was bought, and everyone sees the same town around it.

You can take any of a room's own furniture out of your house, including the new towns' food, tableware and clutter. Before this fix, some of those pieces couldn't be taken out online, and came back after a load offline. Some cabin pieces on Detailed Ships' ships had the same problem.

The two mods place pieces from other mods that this game doesn't include. This game draws its own versions instead of leaving gaps: coloured beds, framed paintings, tapestries and banners for the regions and the Eight Divines, beams, mantels and chimneys, food, animals and tools, rocks and hills, market stalls, docks with their ramps and steps, temple gardens, and crop fields that change with the climate and turn to stubble in winter.
Detailed Ships' bottles and other items now also appear in the towns, even with Detailed Ships switched off.

A few pieces are left out because they're effects, or because nothing is known of their shape, the same as in Daggerfall Unity without those mods. These include some bridges, chimney smoke, and the temples' deity statues.
**Roleplay & Realism:** you can rest in the towns' coloured beds.
**Roleplay & Realism:** the Master Armorer quest finds the armorer's shop in the new towns, instead of naming a neighbour's house.
The bank no longer offers a house that has no door.
Lamps, food and animals in the new towns are no longer mistaken for people you can talk to.
The Mages Guild in Bubandanis and both guilds in Tulaedax work properly.
Buildings in a few new villages now use the right colours and materials for their climate.
Loading a save made inside a building in the new towns puts you back inside it, even after changing which mods are on.
Windmills stand on the new farms when Windmills of Daggerfall is on, and the Order of the Raven's guild halls work in the new cities.
You can enter the castles of Daggerfall, Sentinel and Wayrest in the new cities.
The temples in two village layouts no longer have their front doors blocked by their foundations.
A building no longer fails to load when it holds something the game has no picture for. Nothing is drawn there instead.
Fixed a crash some online players hit right after logging in ("can't access lexical declaration before initialization").

Online homes and guild halls on the block in Daggerfall city where the Arena now stands move to a new house on their owner's next login. Before, the move could miss and the home looked deleted. Nothing was lost; the homes were never deleted.
The arena crowd sounds like people now instead of static.
Fixed the crackle and pop at the end of a match, after the victory celebration.

When you host or join a private session, chat now confirms you're in it and how many others are there. Players watching from the stands aren't drawn, so the arena can look empty. Open Bouts in the Arena window to see who has joined; the host calls fighters to the sand.

An **Arena** button appears on screen during a private session, and the **/** key does the same. Both open the session's Bouts page, so the host can pick fighters and start bouts without going through the pause menu.
Removed the static under the crowd's cheers and boos.
Fixed the crackling after a bout ends. The crowd now roars at the result instead.
Losing a bout no longer kills you or throws you out of the arena. You fall, the healers come, and both fighters go back to the stands.
Watchers in the arena's stands can no longer jump down onto the sand during bouts. A private session's host can still go down, and fighters called to the sand are unaffected.
Players in the arena's stands are now visible to each other and to the fighters, in private sessions, player bouts and the hourly exhibition. In a private session, only its members see each other.
Host and Join now ask you to sign in and be online first, instead of putting you in an empty arena.
Blows in player-versus-player arena bouts land again. Since spectators became visible, your hits could aim at someone in the stands instead of your opponent.
Hits in player-versus-player arena bouts now land every time. They could still go to a nearby spectator instead of your opponent.
The arena floor (bouts and private sessions) now shows the sky above the stands, instead of black.
The Arena of Daggerfall now appears on Daggerfall's town map, drawn as a ring around its sand and labelled "Arena".
Arena buttons and messages are shorter and easier to read: Bet, Find match, Host, Join, Cancel bout, Replay.
The Herald, recruiters and bookmaker offer short, plain choices.
Private session messages say plainly what happened and what to do.
Staff teleport takes you to the right interior in towns with the new layouts.
Teleporting to a boat or cabin keeps you on the right boat and in your own cabin.
Private rooms and homes still check ownership when you teleport or visit.
The save screen no longer leaks memory from its screenshots.

**Search things in dungeons and graveyards.** Coffins, sarcophagi, shelves, chests, crates and graveyard headstones can be searched. You find gold and items, wake undead (sometimes an elite), or find nothing. Each one can be searched again after five game hours. Some chests and crates are locked; pick them in Steal mode.
**Searching in a party.** You get two foes per player, and a search counts for the whole party: everyone sees the same find and waits the same five hours.

**Pace near enemies.** The travel panel has a second speed setting that shows up when enemies slow the clock. It sets how slow travel gets near them. It starts at ×5, so travel no longer drops to walking pace when an enemy is near; set it to ×1 for the old behaviour.
**Spell icons.** In the spellbook, the Icon button lets you pick any icon for a spell. You can also choose no icon; the spell then shows its initials.
**Steady shadows** switch in the Enhanced lighting tile (Settings, Features). It's on by default. There's also a shadow debug log switch, off by default.
Normal enemies drop at most 3 items, gold included (5 in an Elite Dungeon). Their drops are mostly white, blue is rare, yellow very rare and orange almost never.
Champions no longer always drop a Rare. Their Magic and Rare chances are half a normal enemy's, and their Legendary chance is the same as before.
An elite's extra Rare chance is half a champion's at its level.
**Shadows no longer pop on and off** with Enhanced Lighting. Every shadow is redrawn every frame.
The nearest twelve lamps keep full shadows (it was eight), so your shadow and the townsfolk's don't vanish when a lamp swaps in.
Lamps at almost the same distance no longer trade shadows back and forth.
Your own shadow no longer jumps from lamp to lamp.
While Steady shadows is on, your eyes adjust to light changes more slowly, so a brief shadow pop doesn't make the whole screen brighten and dim.
Steady shadows costs more graphics card work and about 48 MB more graphics memory. Turn it off if your frame rate drops.
Fixes and improvements.

**Rest at a rest point.** Online you rest at a lit fire (your Campfire, a friend's, a tent's, a brazier or a dungeon's campfire), at a bed (a rented room, your house, a ship's cabin) or in a guild hall that lets you rest. Out in the open with none of these, the rest window says "Find a fire or a bed to rest." In town, resting outside is still illegal: the window says so, and no guard is called.

**Hold still for six seconds.** The rest window shows a short bar instead of the hours. Press Esc (or Stop in the enhanced window) and nothing happens. The rest is broken the moment an enemy comes, you are hurt, or the fire you rest by goes out.
**Monsters can still find you in the night.** If one turns up while you sleep, you wake at once to fight it, with only the hours you slept behind you - even in the night's last minutes.

**A night passes at once.** When the bar fills you sleep a whole night: eight hours on your character's own clock, in one step. Spells wear off, hunger and sleep work as they did for eight hours of rest, and a rented room's night is used.

**One night every ten minutes of play.** Resting again sooner is a short rest: it heals you, and no time passes. The enhanced HUD's status bar shows a **Rested** tile with the minutes left until the next night.

**One night every ten minutes of play.** Resting again sooner is a short rest: it heals you, and no time passes. The enhanced HUD's status bar shows a **Rested** tile with the minutes left until the next night.
**A night at a fire, a tent or a bed heals you fully.** A guild hall's floor is a rough night with Climates & Calories: in Hard it heals less and you wake stiff.

**Rooms count nights.** A room rented for three days gives three nights, and playing between them no longer uses them up. It still ends once three days have passed for your character, and if it runs out partway through a night you only get the hours you slept.
**A Campfire you leave in a dungeon, lit or cold, comes out with you** with the fuel it has left - when you walk out, are teleported out, or log off down there (offline too).
**The loiter option is gone online.** The sky runs on real time, so waiting for it does nothing.

**Online, every new character starts with a Campfire,** and General Stores sell two to four, whether or not Climates & Calories is on. Pawn Shops have up to two. A Campfire costs 40 gold, half that online, as a potion does. (Offline the Campfire is part of Climates & Calories: a new character with it starts with a full one, and a General Store has two to four on its counter, where it had one to three Campfire Kits on every shelf.)

**Online, every new character starts with a Campfire,** and General Stores sell two to four, whether or not Climates & Calories is on. Pawn Shops have up to two. A Campfire costs 40 gold, half that online, as a potion does. (Offline the Campfire is part of Climates & Calories: a new character with it starts with a full one, and a General Store has two to four on its counter, where it had one to three Campfire Kits on every shelf.)

**It has eight nights of fuel.** Placing it costs nothing. A night you sleep at your own Campfire uses one night of fuel; a friend sleeping at your fire costs you nothing. Firewood refuels it - a smith won't. (Online, until Firewood arrives, a Campfire that has burned its last night is replaced by buying another.)

**It has eight nights of fuel.** Placing it costs nothing. A night you sleep at your own Campfire uses one night of fuel; a friend sleeping at your fire costs you nothing. Firewood refuels it - a smith won't. (Online, until Firewood arrives, a Campfire that has burned its last night is replaced by buying another.)

**Field Cook** (Cooking's choice at rank 50): a night you sleep at your own Campfire uses none of its fuel. (It used to light a Campfire Kit without using a charge; placing a Campfire is free for everyone now.)
**It doesn't burn away.** When it burns down it goes cold and stays where it is. Relight it while it has fuel, or pick it up: it goes back in your pack with the fuel it has left.
**Tents work the same way.** Pitching one is free; a night you sleep at your own tent uses one of its uses.

**Use the loot window's list on a fire.** Look at a fire or a tent and the item list shows what you can do: Rest here, Cook food, Relight the fire (Stoke the fire for a tent), Pick up the Campfire (Pack up the camp for a tent). The highlighted row is what a click does. Online a cold fire offers no rest - relight it first. A brazier's or a hearth's list is Rest here and Cook food, indoors too.

**Dungeons have campfires of their own**: one near the entrance, one deep inside, and more in between, at least 80 metres apart. A small dungeon has one or two, a large one up to seven. An elite dungeon has half as many. A palace, the Burning Court and the Arena's sand have none. A brazier already by the entrance counts as its fire.

They are the same in every player's game, never go out and can't be picked up. They stand clear of loot piles and the way in, light the room around them, you can cook at them, and online you can rest at them.

**Online, no wandering monster appears within 15 metres of one** - for everyone resting there, not only the dungeon's host. A monster that was already in the dungeon can still walk up. (Offline, resting is as in Daggerfall, so monsters can still find you there.)
They show on the compass in yellow, and on the held dungeon map (the enhanced map) once you've seen the spot.
They appear offline too, as places to cook and warm up with Climates & Calories.

**No more votes.** Online, when a party member sleeps a night at a rest point, everyone in the party within 15 metres (indoors, in the same building) who has "Rest with my party" on sleeps that night too, each with their own healing. Only the player who rested can be ambushed, and a rester with "Rest with my party" off carries nobody.
**You sleep by their fire.** Standing near the party member who rested is enough: you sleep as well as they do, not as if you were on the bare ground.

If you're fighting, swimming, in a menu or already resting, you're skipped, and told so - and so are you if you stand in town, where camping is illegal. If you're in the same place but further than 15 metres away, you're told that you missed the night. A night cut short says so.
**A party member's night carries you once,** however their connection behaves; it can't be repeated to keep you asleep.
**In taverns, temples and guild halls everyone rests for themselves,** as before - nobody is pulled into another member's night there.
**/ready now just says how a party rests online.**
**Other players never stop you resting at a fire or a bed.**

**Bedroll** (10 nights): online, once the supplies arrive, a rough rest point wherever you could place a camp, dungeons included - you lay it down and the rest starts after ten seconds; other players nearby still stop you. (Offline every rest is already possible anywhere, so it isn't sold offline.)
**Ember Jar**: lights a fire for one night (about three hours of the world's time). You can rest and cook at it. It can't be picked up.

**Firewood**: adds three nights of fuel to your Campfire, up to eight. It feeds the emptiest of your own Campfires you're standing by, relighting it if it has gone cold; otherwise the emptiest one in your pack that has room.
**Restorative Tonic**: restores 40% of your fatigue at once. With Climates & Calories it also takes four hours off your need for sleep.
**Meditation Candle** (3 uses): light it from your pack, then rest. You kneel for six seconds and get half your magicka back.

**Waking Salts** (3 uses): for an hour, being tired, drowsy or exhausted has no effect. You still get more tired, and two more hours of tiredness hit you when it wears off. You can't take another dose until the first wears off.
**Sleeping Draught**: your next night sleeps as well as a bed, even on the ground.

**Offline** (with Climates & Calories) General Stores and Alchemists sell them (all but the Bedroll), dungeon piles sometimes hold an Ember Jar or a Tonic, and enemies an Ember Jar. **Online they arrive in a later update.** This update teaches every game what they are first, so nobody on an older version loses one in a trade or a shared chest. A character you bring online keeps these supplies on the offline copy for now, and the realm says so.

**Online, a quest that only makes you wait moves on after a couple of minutes of play:** a letter, a meeting, a "come back in three days". Deadlines still run on the world's clock while you play, as the quest timer notes say.
a knightly order's artifact hunt (it no longer ends a couple of minutes after the knight's reward);
the scholar's errand ("Please be prompt") and the banker's lead to the guard;
a noble's daedra heart: you have the chemist's days to come back for your reward (the quest had failed a couple of minutes after you delivered the heart);
the main quest's chapter in Orsinium: it stays there for its six days of play before the Necromancers steal it (it was stolen a couple of minutes after you took the quest);
a thief's delivery "as soon as possible": the contact waits its time for you.

**Quest time limits are back online.** "You have 14 days", travel-time limits and the rest work as they do in Daggerfall again: a deadline can run out. This undoes the update that made online quests time-free.

**A quest that only makes you wait moves on after a couple of minutes of play.** A letter, a meeting, a "come back in three days" arrives about two real minutes later online, and its text says "a few days". Only a quest's deadlines keep their days.
**Quest timers run while you play.** A quest day is about two real hours of play (the sky's day is one).

**Resting, waiting and travelling don't use up a quest's timers online.** An eight-hour rest, a long wait or a fast-travel journey takes nothing off a quest's clock. Only time you spend playing counts.
**Time logged off never counts,** and a tab left in the background counts only its first couple of minutes.

**Countdowns are back** for a quest's deadlines in the journal, the quest tracker, the quest rail and the map markers, along with the "running out of time" warnings. Quest text says a deadline's real number of days again.

**Bounties lapse again** a day after you take them: about two real hours, whether you rest, play or log off. A bounty you held before this update gets a fresh day from your first moment online, kills kept, and one you bring online from offline keeps the time it had left.
**Quest letters wait for morning again**, as well as for you to be in town.
**Vampire, werewolf, Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood quests** still come after a few minutes of play online, one at a time (a cure can take ten or so), as they have since quests went time-free.

A failed quest online still doesn't cost its faction the standing Daggerfall takes for any unfinished quest - but now that deadlines can run out, a quest's own penalty for failing it (some cost standing with someone) applies.

**Ordinary foes drop half as much.** A foe that is not an elite, an Elite Dungeon foe or a champion now leaves each item it would have dropped only half the time, online and offline. Its gold is untouched, and elites and champions drop everything as before.
**A need's tile says how bad it is.** On the enhanced HUD each Climates & Calories need tile shows its stage at its foot ("2/3" is Hungry, of Peckish, Hungry, Starving).
**Every ship takes 60% more punishment.** Hulls and sails are 1.6 times as strong, and cannon balls, fires and rams thin crews 1.6 times more slowly.
This goes for your boats and for every pirate, merchantman and navy ship.
Sea fights last longer and leave more time to manoeuvre, brace and board.
**The odds of a fight haven't changed.** A ship that outguns another still does, by the same margin. A fight costs about as many men as before; it just takes longer.
**Floating casks last longer.** Casks and wreckage now float about 4 minutes (it was 2½), so loot from the first ship you sink is still there after the second.
**Pirates break off at the same point in a fight.** A beaten pirate tries to run for about as long as before she has to strike, instead of 1.6 times as long.
A ship saved whole loads whole, and one saved half-holed loads half-holed.
A part-used Carpenter's Store keeps its work.

A save made now loads in an older version with your boats as you left them, with one exception: the Fleet ledger (below) is new, so in an older version a laid-up ship is gone and a placed one can't be picked up.
**Your crew gets to work sooner and works faster.** The free patch-up starts 15 seconds after the last hit (it was 30) and runs twice as fast. Carpenter's Stores repairs run twice as fast too.
**Your crew gets to work sooner and works faster.** The free patch-up starts 15 seconds after the last hit (it was 30) and runs twice as fast. Carpenter's Stores repairs run twice as fast too.
**No orders needed.** Once a fight is over, your crew uses the Carpenter's Stores in your hold to repair her to full on their own.
Your First Mate says when she's sound or when the stores run out.
Damage below half strength is left to the free patch-up, so no store is wasted on work the crew does for free.
A wrecked Small Ship is whole in about three minutes this way, on 7 stores.
To turn this off, go to Features > Naval Combat > **Crew repairs on their own**.
**A crewed ship repairs even when you're not aboard.** A boat with no crew (a Large Boat you sail alone) is only repaired with stores while you're on her.
**Make repairs is the fast option.** Your crew uses stores from the first plank: a wrecked Small Ship's hull is whole in about a minute and her canvas half a minute later, on 12 stores.
**Damage control.** With an enemy close by, **Make repairs** keeps your crew working at an eighth of the usual pace.
That makes good about a third of the damage a ship your size deals you, at the cost of a store every minute or so.
Fires keep burning while they patch, and a wreck stays crippled until the fight is over.
**The shipwright charges about the same.** He charges less per point because hulls have more points.
Carpenter's Stores cost 314 gold (they were 336) and each one repairs more, so a wreck still takes thirteen (a Carrack now takes eighteen, up from seventeen).
**A sunk ship leaves her wreckage afloat** beside her floating casks. It's larger and paler than a cask.

**Sail through it to haul it aboard.** It gives Carpenter's Stores for your hold (2 from a sloop, 4 from a brigantine or a cutter, up to 6 from a pirate flagship) and powder that fills your stern's fire barrels.
**Sink what you meet and you can keep sailing.** Salvage lets you repair to full and refill your fire barrels without making port.
**If you're swimming,** the stores go into your pack one at a time (or straight aboard, if you're alongside your own boat). Whatever is too heavy to carry is lost, and you're told.
**If you fast travel or go through a door first,** your crew stows wreckage from ships you sank, just as it does the casks.

**Online:** everyone in the room sees the wreckage, and whoever reaches it first hauls it in. A ship sunk in a sea run by a player on an older version leaves no wreckage, and players on an older version don't see it.
**The pause menu has a fourth tab: Holdings**, between Stats and System. It holds everything you own and everyone who follows you.
**Stats is just your character sheet again** (and your Professions, online). The Companions, Revenants and Stores pages moved to Holdings.
**On a narrow window** (a phone), the tabs shrink to fit instead of being cut off.
**Two new pages:** the Stable and the Fleet.
**See your horse and wagon at a glance:** whether you're riding, whether they're following you, or how far away they're parked or waiting.
**Summon** brings them to your side, as the summon key does.
**Send away** takes them back to the stable, out of the world. Mount them from the Transport window any time, or summon them again.
**Rename your horse** right on the page. Renaming with an empty name tells you he keeps no name, not that you don't own a horse.
**Ship deeds no longer sit in your pack.** A ship's title goes into your Fleet ledger.
A deed you buy at a shop goes there the moment you buy it, and she waits for you at that port.
A ship you take as a prize goes there when you claim her.
Deeds already in your pack move into the ledger the first time you open the Fleet page.

**Picking a ship up puts her parts in your pack, and her title goes with them.** Her parts are her: sell them and you've sold her; drop them or chest them and that's where she is. Placing her parts puts her title back in the ledger. Parts can't be placed while that ship is already afloat.
**Each ship gets a card** showing:

**Summon:** at any port (within Come Sail Away's port search range), she's brought round to a free berth at the quay. If the harbour has no free berth, click the water to place her, as a deed did. A Large Galley is too long for a quay, so she's always placed by clicking.
**Send away:** she sails for the port nearest you and is laid up there, cargo and all. A boat with no crew has to be sent from close by. A Large Boat keeps the rig you gave her.
**Repair, even when you're away.** If she has crew aboard, they mend her where she lies, at no cost up to half strength. Past that they use the Carpenter's Stores in her hold.
**Shipwright:** at a port, open the shipwright's window for a ship that's laid up or lying there.
**Hold:** carries 20% more cargo per tier before she rides low.
**Rigging:** 4% faster under sail per tier.
**Hull:** 10% more hull and canvas per tier.
**Guns:** her cannon balls do 8% more damage per tier.
**Refits cost gold and materials from the world**, taken from your pack or her hold:

**A ship bought on the bank's credit can't be refitted** while that region's bank is owed anything (borrowing more, or the Empire calling the debt in, doesn't free her). Once it's repaid, she's free for good. This includes a Rowboat bought as parts.
**Bigger ships cost more:** half the price for a Rowboat, two and a half times for a Carrack.
**Give any ship a name** (up to 24 printable characters). It shows on her hover plaque, for you and for every other player who sees her.
Names go through the same filter as player names.
**Give each named hand a post** from his ship's card: First Mate, Bosun, Gunner, Carpenter, Lookout, Cook or Deckhand. A Bard can keep or return to his calling.
**Each post has a place on deck:**
**Hands keep to their posts** most of the time, and still wander, work and talk now and then.
**With no Lookout named,** a hand with no post keeps the bow, or else a Gunner. A Bard never keeps the lookout.
**One First Mate per ship.** Making a new one makes the old one a Deckhand. Your First Mate is the one who answers you.
**Port towns have quays.** Every berth of a port's harbour now has a timber quay on piles, with:
**They appear as you sail in.** A port's quays stand from about 1.6 km out, so you see them before you reach the berth.
**The port's own ships lie alongside them**, small and large, instead of out in open water.
**Dock your ship.** Strike your sails and come in slowly beside a free quay, roughly along it. Your crew warps her in and makes her fast.

**A gangway runs out** while she's made fast, square to her side: up to a ship's entry port, or down from the quay's edge onto a boat's gunwale. Use it from the quay to go aboard, or from her rail beside it to step ashore. Looking at her helm, hold or door, Activate uses those instead.
**The Fleet page knows where she's docked:** "Made fast at Wayrest's quay", even from far away.
**Summoned ships arrive at a quay,** made fast and ready to board.
**Set sail or take the oars** to cast off.
**Galleys don't dock.** A Large Galley is too long for a quay.
**Online:** every player sees the same quays, except that players with Iliac Puddle's Deep Waters set differently may find a harbour's berths in different places.
**New title: Aegis of Oblivion**, in violet that rises out of the void into a pale lilac light. It belongs to Sureme: press it on the account card to wear it.
**A new glyph comes with it**: three pillars standing through a ring, with the void's tendrils spreading beneath them. It shows beside Sureme's name.

**New aura: Oblivion Ward**, Sureme's own. A whole ring of violet light circles the ground where you stand, with two bright scribes running around it and a bezel of fine ticks outside it. Inside the ring, a circle of twelve runes turns slowly the other way and lights up one rune after another, as if it were being written. Four claws hang from the ring at the diagonals, a violet mist turns inside, and a low veil of light with rising motes stands up off the ring.

**Floating symbols**: runes lift off the ring and float up to chest height, swaying and drifting outward and always turned toward you, then blur, break into dust and fade away. Each one rises again somewhere else round the ring with a new rune.
When the ward is first put on, it draws itself round from behind you. Wear it or take it off from the account card. Every player near you sees it.
Dagon's Fire looks exactly as it did.
Online, every General Store now sells a **Materials Bag** for about 500 gold. It holds 300 kg of crafting materials.

On the enhanced inventory the bag opens beside your pack, like the cart. If nothing else is open beside your pack, use the **Materials Bag** button at the bottom of your pack. On the classic inventory, reach your bag from the Stores page.
Anything you gather goes into your bag first, then your pack. With no bag, it all goes into your pack. Anything that doesn't fit is left where you gathered it, and the game tells you what was left.

**Your Stores are now kept in town.** In any town, open the Stores page (on the pause menu's Holdings tab) to put materials in (one material at a time, or **Put everything in**) or take them out into your bag or pack.
**Empty your bag into your pack** from the Stores page, anywhere.
Crafting stations use what you carry, including what's in your wagon. If your Stores are short, the rest is moved in from your bag and pack. Goods bought with gold on the market are never moved in.
You can't sell or drop the bag while it has anything in it, and it can't be traded.
Food in the bag spoils, just like food in your pack.
The Guild tab is now split into pages: **Overview, Members, Treasury, Vault, Arms and Settings**, and **Stores** where professions are on.

**Rename your guild:** the guildmaster can change the guild's name or tag for 25,000 gold. The gold comes from the treasury, from gold your members' online characters put in. Renames are limited to one every two weeks. You can't rename in a week your guild is in a siege or a Tourney. Your guild's past entries in the Chronicle keep its arms.

**The guild vault:** 50 item slots, or 100 if your guild has bought a hall. Put items in and take them out in any town. By default, officers can take items out 10 times a day, and members and recruits can put items in. The guildmaster can grant or revoke each member's access and set their daily limit. The chest in your guild hall now opens the vault.

**Richer arms:** 16 new devices (40 in all), 7 ways to split the field into two colours, and a colour of its own for the device. Pick them from pictures on the Arms page. Guild banners, shields and tags all show them.
Players who haven't reloaded the game since this update see no arms for a guild that uses a new device, and see split fields as plain.
Guild names and tags now go through the name filter, and a refused name says which word was refused. Names with numbers in them, like "The 22 Blades", are allowed.
Trees in Beautiful Villages towns no longer float. Some village and tavern blocks plant trees on hillsides, and those trees now stand on the hill or ground drawn beneath them.

**Quest-givers are back.** You can hand in a quest you took from a shopkeeper, innkeeper or librarian before the town update. The quest-giver now stands in the building your journal names, as the town is laid out now, and answers to their own name. This also works for party members you shared the quest with.

**Shared quests pick the same monsters.** Every party member's copy of a shared quest now picks the same random monsters, so The Exterminator's vermin no longer switch kind partway through. A party member's quest monsters also no longer fail to appear in a building or dungeon just because the player who shared the quest is nearby. The spiders keep coming in the guild.

**The Totem rises with its cage.** The Totem of Tiber Septim now rises with its cage in Castle Daggerfall's treasury, so you can finish "Who Gets the Totem" again. This works even if another player raised the cage long before you arrived.

The item maker no longer accepts Aetheric pieces: Ruhn's Regalia, the Sigil Broker's Regalia and the raid sets. These pieces carry their own powers, and the maker was laying its enchantments on top of them. Pieces enchanted before this change keep what they have.

Leaving your ship's cabin no longer strands you in a black void. Your ship stays outside while you are below deck, so her own decks no longer cut through the cabin floor and items no longer sink into the gaps. If a save already has you stuck, type `/unstuck` in chat to return to the deck.

Resting again before the next night is allowed now clears lost sleep too. If a night was cut short (an ambush in its first hour), slept on rough ground, or started deep in sleep debt, you can rest again at the fire or bed straight away to shake off **Tired**, **Drowsy** or **Exhausted**. Before, you had to wait out the ten minutes. A rest between nights still moves no time.

**Fixed: logging in sent you straight back to the title screen.** After two server restarts on October 4, everyone reconnected at once and the account service fell over under the load: sign-in failed and dropped you on the title screen. The service now does far less database work on every request, so a full server of players can log in together again.

**Ports show on the Enhanced world map.** Every port you've discovered has an anchor at every zoom, including the whole-bay view the map opens on. Before, anchors appeared only zoomed in, and only with Travel Options' "Only From Ports" on.
**Easier to spot.** The anchor is drawn darker, with a light outline, so it stands out on a busy coast.

**No more ships inside your ship.** A ship you leave made fast at a port's quay keeps her berth while she's out of sight. Before, sailing back into that port could find one of the port's own ships moored right inside her.
**Summon and docking agree.** Neither brings a ship to a berth where one of yours lies unseen.
**Online:** another player's ship lying at a berth keeps it even while its captain is invisible at her helm.
Dying online now costs a tenth of the gold you carry, down from a quarter.

Online, every trip over land on the travel map is travelled rather than instant. Travel Options, its Cautiously and Inns options, and "ships only from ports" are always on online. Ships from a port and travelling to your party leader work as before.
With Climates & Calories on, rations in your pack are eaten automatically when you get Hungry, instead of waiting until you are Starving.

City walls no longer have gaps next to their corner towers. With Beautiful Cities on, the walls of most cities (Alik'ra and Chesterwark among them) had a 3-metre opening on each side of every corner tower that you could see and walk through. These now hold a matching section of the wall.

**A bank ship's cabin goes to the right ship.** If you own a bank ship and more than one sailing ship of its size, the game asks which ship gets the bank ship's cabin (**Link existing bank cabin** on the ship's menu). Before this fix, a ship laid up in your Fleet didn't count. The cabin and everything in it could move into whichever ship was afloat.
When your linked ship isn't in the water, the message now tells you to summon her from **Holdings > Fleet**. It used to point to a deed that is no longer kept in your pack.
Gathering without a Materials Bag puts everything you gather in your pack, even if that takes it over its weight. Before this fix, anything that didn't fit was lost.
When a harvest takes your pack over its weight, the message says so. To lighten it, put materials in your Stores in any town, or buy a Materials Bag at any General Store.
Every shelf in a General Store now sells the Materials Bag. Before, only one shelf per store had it, and it could vanish from that shelf for everyone in the store.
Materials Bags and Campfires never sell out: buy as many Campfires as you like.
Shops no longer buy Materials Bags or Campfires back.
You can only carry one Materials Bag. Trying to buy or pick up a second says "You already have a Materials Bag."
Choosing a category (Weapons, Armour, crafted goods, auctions) no longer hides listings that sat behind 500 cheaper items of other kinds.
Long journeys across the map are no longer refused as "no way by land" when a route exists.
Fast travel remembers the speed you chose. A path's slower cap no longer overwrites it, and the speed panel and the actual clock now agree.
A landfall with no safe shore stops the journey and keeps your boat in the water, instead of packing it away under you.
After a mantle under a low ceiling, you stand up again once there is room, instead of staying crouched. A crouch you chose yourself is kept.
Finishing a vault on a slow frame no longer leaves your hands gripping the air.
Climbing a boat's ladder no longer carries your fall or momentum onto the deck, so you stop sliding off.

Settling a captured ship returns you to your own deck, or to the boat of the player you rode in with. If there is no safe deck to return to, scuttling and casting adrift are refused rather than leaving you in the sea.
"Open her hold" no longer flashes back to the plunder window; when the hold can't open, the window says so.
Players riding another's boat are marked on the travel map where their boat is.
Guild and faction reputation now recovers over time away, even when the clock catches up before your faction data has loaded.
Switching accounts no longer carries the last account's found Motherlode over to the next.
Daedric (and other) weapons show their own model: a longsword is no longer drawn as a katana, or a mace as a club.

**The Small Ship is a brand-new model by Mac.** That is the galleon you can buy, and the hull the pirate brigantines, merchant galleons and navy cutters sail. She has a deep hull with a sharp bow, six oak beams carrying her main deck, and every texture at 64x64, the size of Daggerfall's own.

**Doors and hatches that open and close.** Both hatch covers on her main deck lift open, and a ladder runs down under each one to her gun deck. The door into her great cabin and the door in her gun deck's bulkhead swing open and shut. Use them like any boat door.
**A wheel at the helm.** Her wheel stands on the castle roof, where you steer from, and turns with the rudder as you put the helm over under sail. Under oars the wheel and rudder stay centred.

**Sails and ropes.** She carries five sails: a fore course, two topsails, a big gaff sail on the main, and a jib. They furl and set, fill with the wind and swing as you trim, and their sheets and braces follow them. Shrouds with ratlines, stays and backstays hold them up.
**Painted properly.** A painted hull with gilt bands, a panelled castle, a glazed stern gallery that glows at night, planked decks, gratings, red gunport shutters and tarred rigging.

**Cannon fire from her gunports.** She has five gunports a side. When you lay a broadside, that side's shutters swing up and the guns run out through the ports, even on a quick click. Each ball leaves from its own port, and each gun kicks back as it fires before it's hauled out again. Other players see your shutters open and your guns run out, and when you leave the helm her guns run in and her ports shut. Ships of hers at sea open their ports when they run their guns out.

**Her castle is part of her deck.** Two staircases climb to the castle roof and the helm. Her crew and boarders can walk up them, so nobody at the wheel is out of reach. Her officer and coxswain keep their posts up there while the hands work the main deck.

**Shots tear the canvas that's there.** A ball through her sails tears them wherever the canvas hangs, however you trim. Chain shot passes through where a furled or shot-away sail would hang. Battle damage takes her highest canvas first: main topsail, fore topsail, jib, gaff, then the fore course.
**At a quay**, her gangway climbs to the entry port in her waist. She stands tall, so it's a steeper climb than the Carrack's. Her carpenter keeps his post beside her hatch.
**Harbours sound for her keel.** Where the sea floor shelves gently, berths and their quays lie a little further from the shore than before, so the ships that moor there can put out and come back in.
**If her model fails to load,** the old galleon takes her place with its own guns, decks, sails, gangway and the shallower water it can reach.

The new galleon carries five guns a side instead of the old one's six, so ships built on this hull hit a little lighter in a broadside. A cautious pirate brigantine is less eager to attack a boat on its own.

That lighter broadside changes who picks a fight at sea. A cautious pirate brigantine no longer goes after merchant carracks, so from level 5 the brigantines' raids are on merchant galleons only. A cautious corsair galley now attacks merchant galleons, so from level 7 you can come across those fights. A cautious brigantine now runs from a navy war galley, and from a crewed Large Galley of yours.
Standing in the water or on a quay right next to a moored galleon no longer counts as being aboard her.
A pirate boarding a prize that lies close to land now comes alongside instead of circling off.

Head to wind with her sails set, her gaff and jib are taken aback and drive her astern: about 4 m/s in a steady wind, nearly half her speed ahead. The helm now tells you you're in irons while she goes astern. Put the helm over or strike sail to come out of it.
A gaff, jib or lateen sail on a ship at sea now bellies away from the wind, on either tack. Before, they always bellied to starboard.

Boarders can cross the Carrack's shut cargo doors, and standing on them counts as being aboard. Boarders follow you through open doors into cabins: the galleon's great cabin and the Carrack's rooms. Bodies on the Carrack no longer drop through her forecastle stair or get lifted onto her forecastle.
Companions now follow the path you actually walked when they can't see you. They go through doorways and round corners instead of walking into the wall beside the door.
Companions keep walking while they turn, so they no longer stop and start on every bend.
A companion that has fallen behind speeds up to keep pace with a running player, so they warp in to catch up less often.
Companions growl and moan far less often: every 18 to 54 seconds instead of every 3 to 9.
When your whole party comes through a door, the portal sound now plays once instead of once per companion.
The ghost of King Lysandus is quieter. His cry of "Vengeance!" plays at 40% volume and at most once a minute.
A carriage, its horses and a driver now wait outside the gates of the walled cities (Immersive Travel by kkgobkk). Talk to the driver and press **Fast Travel** to open the driver's map.
Pick a town or village and pay the fare to fast travel there. The fare is a small daily carriage fee on top of any inn nights, and the trip's days still pass for your character.
Drivers won't take you everywhere. As shipped, a carriage goes to cities, hamlets and villages only, and never puts you on a ship. You can change where carriages go in **Mods → Immersive Travel**.
**Disable Normal Travel** is off by default, so your own travel map works as before. Turn it on to make carriages the only way to fast travel, as the mod's author intended.
Turning Immersive Travel on or off takes effect the next time you start the game.

A driver's carriage is the way to fast travel over land online (a ship from a port is the other fast travel). You pay the fare and arrive in the world's present, and the days pass on your own clock. Every trip you start from your own map is still travelled on foot or horseback, as before.
Online the carriages, the fares and the driver's rules are the same for everyone.
Online, vampires and characters hurt by sunlight can't take a carriage by day, just as they can't fast travel from their own map.

Casting a heal or buff on or near a companion, or a party member, no longer floods the notification panel. "Press button to fire spell.", "Aim at your companion..." and "You cast Heal on Hilda." now show once, then at most once every 10 seconds while you keep casting.
The aim hint always shows again when the spell starts waiting for a target after casting straight away, so an armed spell is never silent.
A party member healing you no longer repeats "Bran casts Heal on you." on every cast.
The Professions page descriptions are shorter and plainer.
Herbalism and Hunting now say the search is on the patch's or body's list, not the act-choice key.
With a Materials Bag, the empty Stores page now says gathered goods go into your bag or pack and are put into the Stores in any town.
A house's price now depends on how much ground it covers and how big its town is: 300 gold a square metre, multiplied by up to 2.75 in the largest cities.
Every home costs between 5,000 and 250,000 gold. For example, a 6 × 6 m cottage in a hamlet costs 10,800, and a 12 × 12 m house in Daggerfall costs 118,800.
Before, prices ran as high as 850,000, and a small house could cost more than a big one.
A guild hall still costs the home's price and half again, so at most 375,000.

"Sell your home for N gold?" now shows what you will really get back: 85% of what you paid, plus any rent you haven't collected. A home bought before this change sells back for 85% of what it cost then.
Online, the bank now buys back a knightly order's free house at 85% of the same online price the door uses. Before, the bank paid Daggerfall's old price, up to about a million.
The free house from a knightly order is never a building another player already owns.
Home and rent prices show thousands separators (45,000 gold, not 45000).
Home and rent lines now say the gold comes from and goes to your account at the Bank of the Empire, which is where it moves online.
Port towns' docks now appear even with Naval Combat or Come Sail Away turned off.
Docks now always connect to the town. With Deep Waters on, every dock used to stand alone out on the water about 80 m from shore; each one now has a pier running to land.
**Shadows no longer go too dark, and candles no longer blow out to white, with Steady shadows on.**
It now falls only from the two lamps nearest you, as with Steady shadows off. Those two are still redrawn every frame, so nothing flickers.

**Calmer eye is now its own switch, off by default** (Settings, Features, Enhanced lighting, beside Steady shadows). It used to come bundled with Steady shadows, so dark rooms stayed dark and candle glare lingered for seconds. Turn it on if the picture still seems to breathe brighter and darker.

New **Nearby quests** switch (Settings, Features, World), on by default. Quests from guilds, temples, nobles and townsfolk now send you to towns and dungeons near where you took them, not anywhere in the region.
At level 1, a quest stays within about 10 map squares, a day or two on foot.
Each level adds 4 squares. By level 15 or so, anywhere in the region can come up, as in Daggerfall.
If fewer than three dungeons of the right kind are close, it picks from the nearest three.
A town quest that needs a building no nearby town has looks twice as far, then anywhere in the region.
Quests you already have keep their places. Off is Daggerfall's pick, unchanged. Online, each player's own switch decides their own quests.

**You can loiter online again, with no camp, fire or bed.** When the rest window can't let you rest (no fire or bed nearby, a town's street, or a building that won't let you sleep), it now offers **Loiter**.
**You can loiter at a fire too:** while settling in to rest, press **3** (or your Loiter key), or click **Loiter Instead**.
Loitering works as in Daggerfall: choose the hours, up to your Loiter limit.
It heals nothing and doesn't count as a night's sleep.
Monsters can interrupt it, and it commits no crime.
Online it doesn't bring on night or shorten a quest's waits.

General Stores and Pawn Shops always stock a **Campfire Kit** and a stack of **99 Rations**, with Climates & Calories on or off. Online they never run out. Offline they sell out until the shop restocks the next day, like the rest of the shelf.
Rations and other food can always be eaten, never refused as "not hungry". They give back stamina by how filling they are (rations about a quarter of your stamina). A putrid one is still refused.
A Campfire Kit can be placed, rested at, cooked at, stoked and packed. Only a fire's warmth still needs Climates & Calories.

Quest items standing on beds, dressers and shelves inside houses can now be picked up. The furniture took the click meant for them, which blocked the Thieves Guild's "The Qualifying Examination": the robes you are sent to steal often stand on furniture.
Shelves in ordinary houses no longer swallow your clicks. They were never usable there.
Quest items lying in the world now show their name when you look at them, and a quest letter reads as "Letter: …" rather than "Parchment".

Taking a quest item with quick loot, the right-click / long-press menu, or the gamepad's X now counts as picking it up. Quests that react to the pickup now advance, such as the Thieves Guild's note tucked in the robes or a letter a foe carries.
In a party with a shared quest, a sync that arrives just as you pick up a quest item, or click a quest character, no longer undoes it.
In a castle while the seats are open, the shelves are always the Hall of Records; a click meant to read no longer sometimes searches the shelf.
A candle or other piece standing on a decor dresser can be clicked past the dresser's mirror.
Roads are painted onto new terrain about five times faster.
**Primarch**, a new title made for GA00250. It is drawn in the same light gold the pause menu uses for names.
**The Primarch glyph**: GA00250's own three-barred cross, shown beside the name in the same gold.

**Golden Radiance**, a new aura: a column of golden light around the character, brightest at the edges so the character stays clear inside it. Golden motes rise through it, and a ring of light with turning rays lies at the feet. The light rises from the feet when you put it on. In first person you see the light at your feet, but your view is never tinted gold.
Wear the title and the aura from the account card.

**Founder title**: if you played before the Founder cutoff in one browser or on one device and made your account somewhere else (the desktop app especially), you now get Founder too, as long as at least one of your characters made it onto the new account (a cloud save, its Renown, or a realm character).

**Other players no longer jump backwards.** Near the edge of an area you hear each player through two servers at once, and a late copy of their movement could pull them back a step. You now follow each player through one server at a time, and switch to whichever one is quicker.
**No more teleporting in sieges, Royal Tourneys, and player homes and ships.** Running players there jumped forward on almost every step. Now they run.

**Smoother players on a rough connection.** After a lag spike, players catch up at no more than twice their speed instead of dashing ahead, and small hiccups no longer make them stop and start. They also no longer freeze for a moment every time their movement arrives.
**A player stepping into a new area no longer snaps back** to where they stood when they first connected.

**Players move at the pace they actually moved.** Every movement update now carries the moment it was sent, so other players are drawn at their own pace rather than the pace their updates happened to arrive. After a hiccup they catch up more gently, and they are drawn a little closer to where they really are.

**A lighter server, ready for more players.** The server now does much less work for each player: reconnecting no longer rewrites your details, moving no longer re-saves your connection, and busy areas pick who hears you without re-sorting everyone on every step. It also stops waiting on a stuck part of the server instead of hanging on it.

**Empty areas go quiet.** When nobody else is in your area, your game stops sending its enemies, its memory of the place and your ship's cabin to the server; the party map only updates while a party member is online; and the regular cloud checkpoint skips a save that hasn't changed. The enemies, the place and the cabin are sent in full the moment someone arrives.

Enemies in the water no longer count as "enemies nearby" while you're aboard a boat. A fish under the hull no longer resets the time speed-up at the helm, stops a journey, slows overworld travel, or stops you resting or making camp aboard. Enemies on your deck or on shore still count, and so does anything while you're swimming.

Campfires and tents placed on a boat's deck now stay on the boat as she sails. If the boat is packed away, put in storage, or its owner leaves, your camp goes back into your pack with its uses intact.

W/S and the up/down arrows now do the same thing at the helm. Each press moves you one step along a single ladder: rowing backward, stopped, rowing forward, sails up, then full sail on ships with square sails. Rowing is now a speed you set rather than a key you hold, and taking in the last sail leaves her rowing forward. A/D and the left/right arrows steer. End, and the helm panel's sails button, still raise or stow all sail at once.
Developers can now stage **the Sun Baby** for everyone online with `/event sunbaby` (end it with `/event sunbaby off` or `/event off`).
The sky turns a bright nursery blue full of drifting flowers, and a big giggling baby-faced sun rises out of the east.
The weather clears while it lasts - no rain, snow or storms - and the land is lit like a sunny day at any hour.
Quest people, foes and items no longer appear under floors, in attics, inside stairs or outside walls in some Beautiful Cities and Beautiful Villages buildings.
34 Arkay temples in Beautiful Villages that were left with no houses are back to their classic layout, so their quests can start again.
A quest whose building moved in the new towns no longer sends you to a tavern or a stranger's house.

Entering some houses (Warvale Village among them) no longer drops you into the void or leaves you in the dark. If a room has nowhere to stand you stay outside ("This house has nothing of value."), and if you ever fall below a room you are put back at its door.
Foes, quest foes included, no longer spawn stuck inside dungeon crates.
The Hall of Records book can always be closed.
Placing a tent or Campfire when you already have four out now packs away your oldest camp and returns its gear, instead of refusing. Characters locked out of camping can camp again.
A house given by a Knightly Order no longer offers "Buy it" at your own door, and other players can no longer buy it.
Crop fields no longer grow through walls and buildings, and the rooftop domes stand at their proper size.
Long sessions no longer pile up GPU memory: places you have left are released after a while.
People, guards and foes no longer pop out of view at the edges of the screen.
Party members who rest together at the same camp now share **one** ambush roll instead of each spawning their own enemies.
While the camp's roll is decided you'll see "Resting with <name>...". Everyone then sleeps the same night, or wakes together if it's ambushed.
An ambush on a resting party tries to keep its distance from every sleeper, not just one.
Party leaders can hand the lead to another online member with **Make leader** in the Party tab. Everyone in the party is told.
