The Valkynaz signatures (the Conquest, the Chaining, the Eclipse) now start at their second phase. The Conquest plants its banners one at a time, and each third burns until its banner falls.
The Last Spellmaster's Arcane Lattice now sweeps the whole floor in strips, rim to rim. Her Final Examination returns later in the fight. A caged player is never struck while the cage holds them.
The Wellhead Wyrm takes flight again from its risen perches, and its breath reaches the far rim of its court.
Garoth's Wellfire is aimed at its target.
Duels keep their lord inside the ring, and ring-filling blows stay out of them.
The Armsmaster's guard glint shows only on lords, and the Wingbeat's lane is warned a second ahead.
The Broken Way. The bridges between sections now break apart. You cross them on Drifts, Beats, Crumbles, Pendulums, Vents and Rails, in every direction. Long bridges break several times.
Forks are real choices. The Low Road has its own platforming, and the High Road keeps time with Beats.

In fight halls, the rooms come before the trial, and the door opens right after it. The trial waits for your party to arrive: its waves, the Scriptorium's quiet and the Deserter all hold until you're there.
Approaches mix two kinds of platforms. Passages have real gaps, Drops really drop, Rails never collide, and Pendulums are checked across your whole jump.
Alcoves sit at the edge of the court, behind a doorway in its wall. Balconies and other fittings are where you can actually reach them.
The running leap is off on the Spire's and the Hour's proven courses, so a jump lands where the course was proven to land.
A collapsing tube in a routed hall starts falling when you reach it, not on a fixed timer.
Falling through a void zone to a lower way sends you back instead of letting you skip ahead. A Drop is never mistaken for the void.
Vents burn for their whole eruption. A Pendulum hits exactly where it is drawn. A Drift's chains no longer pass through floors above it.
Broken bridge ends are drawn closed, and every hall of a large circle shows the outlines of its Beats and Crumbles.
Each room's floor counts as new ground for the toll.
Breaches opened before this update keep their old halls until they end.

Every song in the Elite Breach has been re-orchestrated. String sections, brass, choir and organ now play as full ensembles with stereo width instead of single thin voices, and the war drums are real taiko, kick, toms and snare with weight and attack.

The fights drive harder: driving low strings under everything, the legion's chant, brass blasts at the top of each phrase, cymbal swells into each one, and high string shrieks as a Court reaches its last phase.

The halls between fights build as you go: each one starts sparse and climbs to a peak, in each band's own colour. The Galleries have timpani and fanfares, the Cairn a soul-bell and chant, the Shade a rippling harp and a heartbeat, and the Wellhead anvils.
A trial now breaks down and builds back up. The last two minutes of the count have a ticking clock.

The Spire has its own ambience. The dungeon drips and creaking doors are gone. In their place you hear the roar of the void, a drone in each band's own voice, and in the distance the legion's war horns and drums, daedra roaring, and stone breaking and falling into the abyss.
Each band has its own far-off sounds: a cracked bell, wailing souls, howls and whispers, a forge's hammers.
While a Court's lord sleeps, you can hear it breathe.
A revenant that kills you no longer takes a letter of credit. It never takes gold, and a letter is gold.
If a revenant is already holding one of your letters, it comes back to your wallet the next time you load.
A sworn revenant that deserts gives back any letter it carried.
The death screen now names any letters of credit you lost and what they were worth.
If your character's trading is frozen, the death screen now says that what you dropped was lost outright. Before, it said nothing.

Selling a very large batch of gear at once (for example dozens of Daedric pieces) no longer pays you millions of gold *below* zero. A sale that large now pays its real price, as a letter of credit. A purchase that large no longer pays you either.
While you travel in the Overworld, the land ahead of you loads up to three times faster. Fast travel drops to 1x speed far less often, including on straight roads.
While ground is still loading, the Overworld view may run at about 30 fps instead of 60. Once the land is built it goes back to normal.

Tapping or picking the top line of the Weir Key's window ("Weir Keys: 3 - one will be staked.", or "You hold no Weir Key.") no longer closes the window and leaves the key saying "The Spire already asks where you begin." The line is your key count, not a choice: the window now stays up with its list. The quest warning line under it behaves the same way.
Answering No to "Go without ...?" in the Weir Key's window now brings the list of starts back, instead of quietly closing the window.
Using a Weir Key from your pack now closes the pack so the window can open. Before, the window never appeared while the pack was up.

Every city, town and village now has its own economy online, rated from Destitute to Booming. Hover a town on the Held Map or the Overworld to see its economy, whether its market is rising or falling, how its prices compare with the region's usual ones, and who holds the area.
A Booming town's shops ask up to a quarter less. A Destitute town's ask up to a quarter more, and pay less for what you sell.

What you do in a town raises it: walking its streets, buying at its players' traders, and driving a raid from its gates. Gold spent never moves a town, and each player's part is capped per town per day.
Townsfolk talk about how trade is going in their town. A Booming town holds a second market day each week, and a Destitute one holds a market only every other week.
A town's card names the guilds that hold patronage of the area's guild chapters.
A port town's sea lanes lift its economy: the busier the harbour, the better its town does.
A port's exchange now prices by its town's economy. A Booming port sells goods cheaper, and a Destitute one dearer. The Exchange tab shows the port's economy.
Every deal at a port's exchange raises that town's share of the players' activity, like trading at a player's stall.

On a seat's Market Day, and for a holder's members, shops now pay less for what you sell as well as asking less. Essentials can no longer be bought and sold back for a profit there. A friend's caravan on the road now gives its friend's price both ways.

A shop never pays more for an item than you paid a shop for it, so carrying shop goods from a cheap region to a dear one no longer makes gold. Loot you find sells as before. Improving a bought item (setting a gem, honing, reforging) is now paid for when you sell it.
Materials bought at a shop stay in your pack instead of going into the Stores. Crafting stations still use them straight from your pack.
A gem bought at a shop keeps its shop price when you set it in a socket and when you take it out again.
A town's card now shows two chapter patrons by name and a count of the rest, with the guild holding the most chapters first. It shows them only when the card has room, so it fits on a phone screen.
In the Elite Breach, a bridge that runs above a Gust course no longer blows you off it. A Gust course laid straight after another one, on a different line or height, now gusts as it should.
The Shadow Fang title now carries moderator powers: /mute, /unmute, /ban, /unban, /strikes and the reports' queue. Moderators can't ban or mute a Shadow Fang holder.

Smithing, Building, Outfitting and Provisioning's cooking now say on the Professions page where their stations are, how to work them from the Stores page (press your Professions key, then Holdings > Stores), and what earns XP.
A new Crafting page in Tutorials lists which shops hold which station.
The Professions key's row in Controls now says it opens your Professions page.

Your other characters can now use the crafting stations in a home your account owns, the same as the character who bought it: forge, workbench, loom, mason's and jeweller's benches, alchemy and enchanting. The home's storage still belongs to the character who bought it.
Leap and dash weapon techniques, Flying Kick included, now work from the ground while you wear Slowfalling gear such as The Raven's Wings, and they land where you aim.
The Twin Lords: a Sapper that reaches a fallen twin now crumbles instead of healing it. A fallen twin can no longer get up early, untouchable, while still attacking.
Valkynaz Ilthys's banners can now be broken with arrows and spells from the court floor.
While two banners stand, her health bar shows a hatched "Warded" cage.
The Last Armsmaster's ring of fire is now drawn on the floor, and a solo challenge is told it is fought in the open.
A solo player who defeats him mid-challenge is no longer told the challenge went unmet.
Players who are down or watching see the ring too.
Winch plates are marked in gold.
Boss callouts no longer go silent after a dozen lines in a long fight.

Bodies and their loot no longer come back when you re-enter a dungeon while another player in it has the game in the background. The room now follows whoever is actually playing. A player returning from being away rejoins without overwriting the room.
If that background player's game then closed without saying goodbye (a crash, a lost connection), the room could stay stuck the same way. It now moves on to whoever is playing.
The Controls menu now names the window the L and N keys open. On Enhanced Plus that is the Chronicle, on its Quests or Notes page; on Classic it is the logbook.
The FPS counter now remembers stutters. When a frame took 50 ms or longer in the last minute, a "hitch" line shows the worst one and how much of that frame was the game's own work.
The FPS counter no longer shows "0 fps" after you switch away from the game and come back.
A packed ship's parts now weigh only her hull (120 kg at most). Cargo in her hold no longer adds to that, so storing things in a packed ship's hold can't make her too heavy to pick back up.
Ship parts that were already too heavy to take out of a chest or other storage are fixed when you load your save. Nothing in their hold is lost.
When your character is too weak to carry a ship's parts, the pick-up now says "The ship's parts are too heavy for you to carry." It used to tell you to unload cargo, which didn't help.

Magic items from guild vendors, shops and loot no longer come on wands or holy items when their power only works while worn. An "Enhances skill" or "Cast when held" item is now always something you can equip.
An enchanted jewel that used to be a Wand, held in a guild vault or market listing and turned into an Amulet when you loaded it, no longer gets your character flagged by the anti-cheat check.
The spellbook keeps your place: picking a spell no longer jumps the list back to the top, and the list now scrolls on its own so the spell you picked stays in view beside it (below it on a phone).
The Chronicle keeps its place when you fold a quest or note, remove a note, or share or abandon a quest, and a long Chronicle no longer stalls when you do.
Deleting a spell no longer opens the next one scrolled down to where the deleted one was.

Sweet Mother's Kiss (The Night Mother's Embrace, and any Rare imprinted with it) now gives its +50% against bosses under a quarter of their health: the Oblivion Gate's Warden and his host, the Abyss Dungeon's Remnant, the sea serpent, and every foe in an Elite Breach. Before this it never triggered against any of them.

The same fix applies to the other "under its health" effects against those foes: Serpent's Kiss's double poison, Run Them Down, Gutting Lunge, Headsman's Chop, and the Axe and Blunt Weapon mastery bonuses.
Number keys 1-9 now pick rows in the Use Magic Item list (and other windows) inside dungeons, not just outdoors.

In a dungeon, pressing a number with a window open no longer fires the hotbar slot behind it (for example, drinking the potion on slot 1), even a number pressed the instant the window opens. The HUD now hides under dungeon windows, as it already did elsewhere, and the keyboard and controller agree on when the hotbar is yours.

The imps that follow you across a span's platforms can't be hurt from the platforms, by design. Your blows there used to look like they landed. Now they ring off with "No footing". Step onto an island or plate to fight them.
Blows that hit a ward (Vengeful Shades, guarded Ward-Bearers, a lord's shield) or a lord still asleep in its ring now say "Warded", and no longer heal you.

Vampiric and leech weapons, the Mace of Molag Bal, spells (Siphon Life and the other path spells), Cast When Strikes and set bonuses no longer heal you or give anything back off blows that deal nothing, including the Warden's shield and the Brass Remnant while it's closed.
A Court lord can be hit the moment it wakes; for up to two seconds your blows used to ring off it.
A foe on a storey above or below you now says "Warded" instead of looking hit, and arrows and spells that land nothing say "No footing" or "Warded" too.
Bushes no longer grow out of house walls in the towns rebuilt by Beautiful Cities and Beautiful Villages, including the one by Penwall Derry's east gate.
World of Daggerfall's rocks, camps, shrines and ruins no longer stand on the low open sea or on the lowest shore of the coastal regions. The mod meant to keep them off, but its check never worked.

The boulders in rebuilt towns and villages, such as the stream rocks in Ipsmoth, are solid again. They had been drawn inside out, as hollow shells you could see through, and their stone texture is no longer smeared. The ramps and steps on the rebuilt villages' docks are no longer drawn inside out either.

Crafting stations now say when the crafter's limit stops a craft's XP. A character raises only two crafts past Journeyman (rank 50); the rest stop at 50. The station now names your two, instead of promising XP it won't pay.
The Professions tab explains the limit before you reach it, and a station's XP now includes your Firmament stars' bonus.

Two crafts finished at the same moment could push a third craft past Journeyman and then freeze all three at rank 50 for good. The service now decides the limit inside each craft, so that can no longer happen.
A craft below 50 shows its next rank's XP again, and a Master's craft no longer claims a first-time bonus it didn't pay.
When the gate opens, its court lets a crowd in about five times faster. If it is busy you now wait at its door instead of being thrown out of the court.

When all 256 places in the Burning Court's fight are taken you are no longer sent away: you stay at its edge and watch the whole fight, and you join it if a place frees (one frees when someone who took a place leaves without really fighting - a fighter who fought keeps theirs). While you watch nothing in the court can hurt you, you cannot strike, and you earn no share of the spoils.

Your online character now saves itself every five minutes instead of every two. Trades, crafting, profession work and everything the server settles still save at once, and the game still saves when you switch away from it - only a crash could cost you up to five minutes of play: walking, looting, quest steps, a level-up.
The account service makes fewer trips to its database, so busy evenings should load faster.
A revenant marked at its lair is now found there: it stands where you can walk to from the entrance, never in a sealed pocket or a cap no path reaches.
A revenant the road had stood goes home to its lair when you visit, instead of standing nowhere - and the road body it left never comes back as the revenant after you deal with it at its lair.
Winning a raid at sea now ends it: the raid's crew and any late wave are removed, so travel, resting and the Overworld no longer say enemies are near.
If the enemy ship leaves the sea mid-fight, its raid's crew goes home with it.
The pirate attack's victory gong rings again.
The wallet's row and card show what its contents weigh; each holding in the wallet shows its own weight. Nothing's weight changed.

A monster handed to you by another player's game is now checked against what the game itself can build. One with health or a level no real spawn could have is removed from your world instead of fighting you, and is never rescaled.
You are never blamed for a monster someone else's game handed you.

The relay now counts the impossible monsters it drops itself, and an account that asks for far more spawns than play allows opens a moderation case on its own. One batch of findings is one line on the case, and the Discord card says the spawn grants opened it.

Morrowind-bodied characters in third person now walk and run on their own legs. Each foot is set down on the ground where it lands and stays there until it lifts, so feet no longer slide. The hips, chest, arms and head move with each step.
The legs follow where the body actually goes. Walk into a wall and the legs stop. Strafe or walk backwards and the legs step that way, for other players' characters too.

Walking, running and sneaking each have their own posture, and sneaking while standing still crouches. Strafing turns the hips toward the direction of travel, walking backwards is a backpedal, and turning on the spot steps the feet around.
The stride fits the pace and the body. Men and women each have their own gait, and Argonians and Khajiit share the beast gait. Every race's height and build sets the stride.
Slopes are walked on the slope. Sudden changes of direction are much smoother: the body dips far less, and the feet no longer jump in the air.
One-handed weapons hang down and away from the side at rest, and a running character carries the blade low with its point trailing behind.
Two-handed weapons are held in a low guard with both hands at rest, and carried at the hip at a run.
Paired weapons are held out from both sides at rest, and swept back behind the body at a run.
Staves and spears are held in both hands on the haft, and bare fists have their own guard.
Wrists stay in a natural range, and blades stay clear of the ground and the body, including between walking and running.

Third-person slashes, chops, thrusts and backhands now use the whole body. The hips and chest turn into the blow, the weight shifts forward, the lead foot steps in, and the weapon leads with its edge.
The weapon moves smoothly through each attack without flipping, and meets its target at close to full speed.
Two-handed blows keep both hands on the weapon. A left-hand blow is the mirror of a right-hand one, and a one-handed weapon held alone strikes with its own hand.
The legs keep walking during an attack, so the body no longer stops mid-stride and slides. An attack that is interrupted, or cut short by the next one, flows into what comes next.

This is on by default. To turn it off and go back to the original animation clips, use the Morrowind Body Motion switch in Settings, under Combat > With Morrowind data. The switch's text is now translated into every language the game ships.

Orcish and Daedric gear no longer drops for brand-new characters as often. Below level 20, an orc's or a daedra's metal drop is often a mid-tier metal instead (Elven at low levels, rising through Dwarven, Mithril and Adamantium to Ebony). From level 20 the drops are as before.
Online, Orcish and Daedric pieces dropped by orcs and daedra, and bounty rewards, now sell for the condition they were found in, even after a repair, like all other loot.
In an online room, an orc's or a daedra's armour drop is now the same for everyone in the room.

Your maximum health is never below what an average roll at every level would have given you with your current Endurance. Raising Endurance later, including from the Firmament's stars, now counts for every level you have already gained. Nobody loses health.
Every level now gives exactly 5 attribute points instead of 4 to 6.
Levelling up online no longer changes your current health.

The Stats page shows how many uses each skill has toward its next point, says when it is ready (and, inside the 6 hours between skill checks, how long until a rest or journey raises it), and says why when it is held (at 100 unmastered, or the 95 lock).
A "Skills can be improved" notice stays on screen while a rest or a journey would raise a skill.

On the Growth tab you can now change one class skill you have not mastered for a skill outside your class, in the same group, for 100,000 gold. Your level and skill values stay the same. A class with only one weapon skill (or school of magic) can now reach a specialisation. The page warns you if the new skill could never be mastered, and an heir keeps the changed class.

On the Growth tab you can now change one class skill you have not mastered for a skill outside your class, in the same group, for 100,000 gold. Your level and skill values stay the same. A class with only one weapon skill (or school of magic) can now reach a specialisation. The page warns you if the new skill could never be mastered, and an heir keeps the changed class.
Guild vault: hover a piece (or tap its name) to see its full item card, base and modifiers included. Filter the vault by name, pack page and rarity. Unidentified pieces keep their names hidden.
Guild vault: hover a piece (or tap its name) to see its full item card, base and modifiers included. Filter the vault by name, pack page and rarity. Unidentified pieces keep their names hidden.
Guild Stores: the put in / take out form is now above the list, leaving Units empty moves all of it, and a new Put in all button empties your Stores into the guild's.
Guild Stores: the put in / take out form is now above the list, leaving Units empty moves all of it, and a new Put in all button empties your Stores into the guild's.

Hammerfell's south-eastern shore, from Lainlyn and Satakalaam east to Mournoth, is now dense jungle: giant trees close overhead with taller ones breaking through, young trees and palms fill the light gaps, and the floor is carpeted in ferns, broad leaves and grass.
A humid haze hangs under the canopy, thickest at dawn and in rain, and it thins as you climb out of it.
On by default: switch it in the Features menu under "The world" ("Jungle of Bantha"). It is always on when playing online.

What falls now depends on the air where you stand: its climate, the season, the hour and your height. Cold peaks get snow, warm lowlands get rain, and sleet falls in between, so one storm can rain in a valley and snow on the ridge above it.
Snow settles where it falls and melts as the air warms. In a thaw, white mountains stand over green valleys.
A hard, smooth arc that could cut across the sky at dusk is gone.

Every crafting station now spells out its quality odds. The old line, *"Your rank 28, margin 18: Standard 50 | Fine 40 | Superior 10. A clean heat is a step better."*, now reads: *"Quality chances: Standard 50% | Fine 40% | Superior 10%. They get better the further your rank (28) is above the recipe's (10). Land every strike while the glow is in the band to raise the result one quality."*
Each station says what its minigame asks for the bonus: the anvil's strikes, the plane along the grain, every stitch on the beat, the chisel on the marked line, the facet that catches the light.
A Tailor's clothing, a Leatherworker's leather and the town Apothecary's bonus are each said in a sentence of their own.
Friendly merchant and navy ships moored at a port's quays can now carry you. Walk up to one, look at her hull and press Activate.
Her captain lists every port you know, nearest first, with the direction it lies and the fare (Daggerfall's ship fare for the whole voyage).
Pick a port and confirm. You board at her helm and the voyage is sailed across the Overworld - never a jump. Nothing is paid until she sets sail.
If the voyage stops (an enemy nearby, a fight, loading a save), her captain sails on by himself while you stay aboard. He keeps to the port you paid for.
At the far port she lands you, and you walk the rest of the way in. Step off her anywhere and the passage ends; anything you put in her hold comes back to your pack.
Online, any player at the port can book a ship there, and once she has sailed she is gone from that berth for everyone for the rest of the day. Other players can board and ride along.
The enhanced inventory has a new Batch salvage button. Tap pieces to tick them, or use All Magic, All Rare or All junk to select in one go.
A sweep never picks a Legendary piece - you choose those by hand.
Pieces that can't be salvaged (worn, locked, set with gems) are dimmed and say why.
One question confirms the whole batch: it lists the pieces and the shards you'll get. Keep cancels and leaves your selection in place.

On by default: on foot you are now drawn in the helmet, chest armor and leg armor you actually wear: leather, chain, or plate in iron, steel, mithril, adamantium, ebony, orcish or daedric. Each character uses its own body.
The profile's Skin card now opens on a Look toggle: Skins or Layered Gearing (WIP).
Layered Gearing lets you choose the Female or Male body. If you switch to Skins and back, it keeps the body you chose for the rest of the session.
A worn Casual or Formal Cloak adds its hood and cape in its dye, over any armor.
On a horse you are drawn in your Mounted skin. As a werewolf or wereboar you are drawn as the beast.
Other players see your Layered Gearing look once the servers are updated. Until then they see your skin.
Settings > Features > Quick slots: Off, Diamond (slots 1-4), Hotbar (the default, ten squares) and the new Diamonds (ten diamond-shaped slots).
With the pack or spellbook open, point at an item or spell and press a slot key to put it on that slot. This works with every bar style.
The game's own text now uses American spelling (armor, color, harbor, specialization, jeweler, catalog).
Instructions and messages are written as plain, complete sentences, with "experience" in place of "XP".
On the enhanced skin the 2 and the Z are redrawn so they can no longer be mistaken for each other.
A journey no longer drops to x1 while the land ahead is still loading. It holds back only as much as needed, and full speed returns as soon as the land is built.
An enemy camp that has not noticed you no longer keeps the Overworld view down and the journey at x1.

Online, mending a looted weapon or piece of armour yourself raises its sell price again. A merchant pays for the condition it was found at, plus a third of what your own repair kits, Repairs Objects and the Varla Stone mended past that.
An enchanted found piece now sells at the Mages Guild for its found condition, not as if it were undamaged.
Hired-trader patrons now pay less for worn pieces, the same way shops do.
Tempering a found piece no longer lowers its sell price.
A worn book you find no longer becomes undamaged when it stacks with, or splits from, another copy.
With Layered Gearing on, you now see every other player on foot in the armor they wear, not only yourself and players who chose it too.
Each player is drawn in the body they chose, or their character's own if they never chose one.

Two-handed weapons such as greatswords, warhammers and battle axes are now carried low at the hip in both hands when running, held out in front of the hip rather than against it. The blade trails behind, and the chest turns toward the weapon.
Running with a one-handed weapon and a shield no longer swings the shield up behind your head. The shield arm keeps Morrowind's own shield pose.
The running stride is stiffer. The knees bend less and the heel no longer kicks up behind, so the body rides higher and more upright.
When running with empty hands or fists, each hand now stays on its own side instead of crossing in front of the chest.
In first person, the running fists come up in front of each shoulder instead of near the middle of the screen.

In the Gauntlet, killing a Caster now silences its pillar. Before, only standing on the pillar's plate counted, and a group that killed every Caster was stuck with "Casters left" never dropping and a door that never opened. Runs already stuck in a Gauntlet get unstuck as soon as this goes live.

A lord no longer gets weaker when members of your company fall. A fallen member's part of the lord's health used to leave with them, so the lord melted under the survivors' blows the moment the team went down. Now the living have to finish what the fallen left: losing members in a Court makes the fight harder, never easier.

A lord is now sized for the members who actually reached its hall. A teammate still on the stairs, or disconnected, when the hall wakes no longer makes the lord tougher for everyone else. They add their part when they arrive, at the health the lord has left, so a late arrival never heals him.
A lord still asleep in its ring when a member falls on the way to it wakes sized for the company still standing.
Descriptions, tooltips, guides and messages across the game have been rewritten in short, plain sentences. Codes and file names no longer show up on screen.
Mod settings now say in a sentence or two what each setting does. Settings that do nothing in this game say "Has no effect".

The credits in the About pane say what each mod and library does for you. Every author, version and license is still named. Two credits were wrong and are fixed: Roleplay & Realism's later parts and Eye of the Beholder's animations, footsteps and cart are already in the game.
In The King's Gambit, "Least stake" is now "Minimum stake".
Every language's translation has been updated to the new wording.
The Elite Breach's windows now use the Enhanced Plus style: the card offer, the run recap, the boards and the call tracker.

On Enhanced Plus, a new start window opens the breach. It shows your Weir Keys, where you can start, which of your company can start there, and up to three decrees to wager. Then choose Open the breach, Rehearse Halls 1-5, Boards or Cancel. If the breach can't open, the reason is shown above the buttons.
Choosing cards: press 1-6 to choose, Y for Ready and R for a respite. Spending a Surplus now reads "draw new cards". Press Enter to close the recap.
Some of these messages come from the game servers. You will see their new wording after the servers are updated.
Every quest in the game now shows its objectives, one at a time. Your journal and the quest tracker name the step you're on, and a herald line tells you when you finish one.

Many quests, the guilds' and the great houses' best-known jobs among them, now ask you to choose how they end: spare the wounded spriggan or finish the job, sell a lich's books to the Mages Guild or burn them as the temple asks. Each ending pays and is remembered in its own way.
Thirteen questlines now run alongside the quests you take at guild halls and taverns. Each opens with a letter or a courier when you're ready for it.

The Dagon Cycle: *The Burning Doors*, *The Covens' Hoard* and *The Weir Road*. Someone is opening Dagon's Breaches on purpose. Follow the trail through the Breaches, the Elite Dungeons and the Elite Breaches to the Valkynaz who guard them.
The Hour That Was Not: the priests of Akatosh feel a wound in time under the Bay. It leads you into the Abyss Dungeons.
The Old Coil: Sentinel's sailors say what the World-Skin shed still swims.

Eight introductions: *The Court Crafter*, *The Smith's Secrets*, *The Harbormaster's Word*, *The Merchant's Road*, *A Seat at the Table*, *The Herald's Call*, *The Bay's Troubles* and *Written in the Stars*. Each shows you one of the game's newer pursuits: crafting, gear, sailing, trade, the tavern tables, the Arena, the Bay's troubles and the Firmament.

A failed step comes back the next day, so a questline never closes on you. If a step needs something switched on (Loot rarity, Naval Combat, The King's Gambit) or a registered account, the questline's page says so.

Quests that pay gear now let you choose one of three pieces made for your class: a weapon in one of your best skills, a piece of armor and a jewel, better the harder the quest. Each card shows the piece's damage or armor, its hands and its weight, and Take asks you to press it twice.
A questline's ending pays a named piece of its own, 22 in all.
Endings with guilds, temples and houses move your standing with them; online, a quest that ends unfinished still costs you no standing.

Online, the Dagon Cycle, the Hour and the Old Coil also pay titles, held by your account: Doorwarden, Covenbane, Weirwalker, Witness of the Hour and Satakal's Witness. The Covens' Hoard can pay a Weir Key, once an account. These are only paid for what the service saw you do: a breach closed, a Redoubt taken, an Hour broken, the Serpent slain.

The Quests window has a new Questlines section. It shows every questline (running, waiting, locked or done), the step you're on and what opens the next one. Each guild you've joined appears there too, as a ladder of its quests by rank. A reward waiting can be reached from the pause menu on either skin.
The questlines are always on in the online world. Offline, they're a Features switch, on by default. The classic logbook is unchanged.

Some nights Dagon's Breach holds more than the Warden. A portent is a third kind of mark beside his aspect and his trials, and it is always announced: in the chat with his marks, on the map's card, on the marks card, and in the Discord omen post. About two breaches in five carry one, and never two breaches in a row. A Legion-Lord night never does.
The Vanguard - *His vanguard holds the approach.* You arrive on a platform out in the fire, with the Warden in sight across it.
The Sundering - *He tears in two at the second phase.*
The Captive - *A knight of the Covenant lies chained in the Pen.*
The Dire Breach - *Dagon's Breach runs deep.* The Vanguard and the Sundering on the same night.

6 seconds after the first fighter lands, the first wave rises from the fire. Each next wave comes when a quarter or fewer of the last still stand, or after 30 seconds. Clear the Bridgehead's 3 waves and a walkway rises to the Muster. Its third wave brings the Markynaz, the Warden's lieutenant. He calls Imps out of the fire every 15 seconds. When he falls his Imps crumble with him; bring down whatever else stands and the way to the Warden opens.

New foes: the Brute (a Daedroth that smashes the ground around it), the Caster (it keeps its distance and throws bolts of the Warden's element at your feet) and the Markynaz (a Daedra Lord whose Rend hits hard and wide).

The waves are sized to how many of you stand on the platform, so a full court breaks them in about the same time as a few. The Warden himself has less health on a Vanguard night, so the night takes no longer than a plain one.
Stall too long (4 minutes) and the Warden tires of waiting: his meteors start falling on the platforms (twice each, if he is Echoing).
The Warden's bar shows where you are: *The Vanguard - Bridgehead, wave 2 of 3*.

On a Sundering night Valkynaz Ruhn doesn't bound to the Burning Court at his second phase. He leaps to his court's heart and calls the Sundering (step out of its 8 m disc), then tears himself in two: Ruhn's Blade, his body, and Ruhn's Flame, his aspect's fire made flesh (Ruhn's Rime, Storm or Venom under his other aspects: an Atronach of fire, ice, iron or flesh).

With 4 or more of you in the fight, the Blade bounds to the Burning Court and the Flame to the third court over the Rift Way, a new walkway. Split up and take both. With fewer, both fight you side by side in the Burning Court.
The Blade keeps his steel (Cleave, Ground Slam, Charge, Leap, Chains). The Flame keeps his fire (Hellfire, Meteor, Flame Nova, Dagon's Brand).

Each half has its own health, shown on its own track under his bar. Bring one down and it kneels for 20 seconds. Bring the other down before it rises, or the first gets back up. It rises with as much health as the other half has left, so the two are even for the next try.
A half left with nobody in its court for 10 seconds starts to mend (its track says *Alone*).
Both down together and the halves rejoin in the first court (keep off its heart: the Rejoining is a 9 m disc). Run back: his last stand as Dagon's Champion is fought there.
Chains of the Warden - a burning chain to one fighter near him. Be more than 16 m from him when it lands or you're dragged to his feet, and a Ground Slam follows.
Dagon's Brand - rings under up to 3 fighters. When it lands, each ring bursts on everyone *else* near it. Branded fighters: get away from the group.
Shared Torment - a gold ring under one fighter. Its blow is split between everyone standing in it, so gather on them. It only comes when 3 or more of you stand before him.
Scything Wheel - 2 blades turn around him for 6 seconds. Stay ahead of them, or out of reach.
The Burning Gaze - nothing on the ground. If you're looking at him when it lands, it hits and blinds you. Look away.
The Unmaking - half his court's wedges burn, then the other half. Step into a dark wedge, then back into one that has already burned.
When one of these is on you, the order shows under your crosshair (Chained! Run from him!, Look away!), with an arrow pointing the way out.
2 to 4 gaolers rise as the first of you steps into the Pen, by how many of you are fighting then. They don't move, but they pulse at anyone who comes near.
Cut them all down and the knight goes free, standing in gold: *The Covenant's ward stands over the court.*

The next Dagon's Reckoning to land breaks on the ward and hits nobody. Its crystals still shatter for the stun if you break them. If you break a Reckoning before it lands, the ward waits for the next one.
The Warden's bar shows *Gaolers: 3*, then *The Covenant's ward* until it's used.

Beat the Warden on a portent night and your spoils carry one more piece of Magic or better for each portent: one for the Vanguard, one for the Sundering, and one for the Captive if the knight goes free. A Dire Breach pays 2. Each such piece can be socketed, carry a technique or turn Exalted like any other. Your Weir Key chance on a night whose portent pays (a Captive night only if the knight goes free) rises from one in six to one in four.

Beat the Warden on a portent night and your spoils carry one more piece of Magic or better for each portent: one for the Vanguard, one for the Sundering, and one for the Captive if the knight goes free. A Dire Breach pays 2. Each such piece can be socketed, carry a technique or turn Exalted like any other. Your Weir Key chance on a night whose portent pays (a Captive night only if the knight goes free) rises from one in six to one in four.

About one breach in five, with no warning, a Tithe-Imp bolts from the fire while the Warden is in his first or second phase: a large Imp burning gold, carrying a tithe to its master. It strikes nobody and runs from whoever is nearest, a little slower than you can run, so expect a chase. Catch it within 22 seconds, before he leaves its court, or it dives back into the fire. Everyone who landed a blow on it gets their own tithe: gold by their level and a gem, straight into the pack.
Your quests' destinations now appear on the Overworld as gold diamonds. The quest you're following is filled in and stays pinned to the screen edge, showing its distance and time left.
Click a quest mark to start a journey there.
Dungeons on the Overworld are slightly smaller and now stay the same size as you zoom in and out.
While travelling, the Overworld tells you what weather you'll run into ahead, and when you'll get there ("Rain ahead - 2.4 km, in 20 min").
When you're standing still, it shows the next few hours' weather where you are. Hover over a place to see its forecast too.
Planned routes now stay on the road from start to finish, including around corners, through towns on diagonal roads, and up to a spot you clicked near a road.
Travel inside a town slows to x5 and follows the streets instead of running into buildings.
If the city gates are shut for the night, your journey stops and tells you why.
You can now see other players being chased by bands from as far away as the bands themselves are drawn.
Weapons held while running no longer wag side to side with your shoulders. Dual-wielded daggers, one-handers, two-handers, staves and spears all stay steady as you run.

Running with two weapons drawn is no longer stiff. Your arms stay swept behind you, but they now pump with your stride and your elbows bend, instead of being locked straight back with your wrists twisted round.
With a two-handed weapon (or a staff or spear held in both hands), your shoulders no longer twist with each step, so the weapon stays still in both hands.
Running is less stiff-legged. Your knees bend and spring more, roughly halfway between the original run and the stiffer one from the last update.

A lantern hung at your waist on the Morrowind body is now a sensible belt-lantern size (about 30 cm). It was hanging at full street-lantern size. It is the same size the Eye of the Beholder sprite's lantern already was.

Every map square of the jungle now stands 48 trees a day for Logging, four times the richest woods anywhere else. Every one of them can be felled: on ground that hasn't been vouched for yet, trees that would be Teak or Mahogany stand as Pine instead of standing nothing.

The jungle's big trees now stand about 16 m apart instead of crowding in every 12 m, and its young trees and palms stand at most one to a patch of ground. That is less than half as many trees, so you can see and walk between them, while their crowns still meet overhead.

Winding dirt trails now cut through the jungle, meeting, crossing and looping, about one through every map square. The ferns and grass keep off them, and the big trees stand back from them as they do from roads.

You no longer walk through trees, rocks, stumps, fallen logs, barrels, crates, statues and other solid props, on foot or on horseback. Walk into one and you slide around it. Grass, flowers, ferns and bushes can still be walked through. If you ever end up inside one (after a teleport, say), you can walk straight out.

Herb patches, veins, boulders, fishing schools, dungeon veins and trees now have a crisp outline in their profession's colour. It follows the outline of the node itself, including the full 3D tree, instead of the faint sparkle in front of it. The outline fades in as you approach, fades with distance and fog, and is hidden by anything standing in front of the node. A skinnable body drawn as a 3D character keeps the old glow.
The jungle floor now carries as much grass as meadows elsewhere, growing between the same ferns and flowers. The ferns and flowers stay at the amount they were thinned to.
The name filter now refuses names containing "prostitute" or "strangler", even when they are run together with another word. In chat, letters and notes these words are starred out.

Ysolde Marnhel, Prior Anselm Vey, Hamid al-Rasheen and Corvane Tull now carry their own names when you meet them. Before, the person you had to find and talk to wore a different, random name from the one the quest's letters, journal and guide gave you, on their nameplate, in the talk window and under the Info cursor. Every quest's people now answer to the name their quest uses.

Weir Keys now stay in your pack. They can no longer be stowed in the wagon or in storage, and keys stowed earlier are cleared when you load. Your account's real key count is unchanged; the extra keys that turned to rust on use were never real.

The item maker takes each side effect's setting once. A drawback such as User Takes Damage in holy places can no longer be stacked for extra points, and an effect with every setting taken leaves the list. Items you enchanted before keep their enchantments.

In the Wrothgarian Mountains a companion's pack is at stake with yours: a death there drops what your crew hand or sworn revenant carries. Companions can't be sent away from inside the zone, and one knocked out there leaves its pack with you.

Disintegrate now works on online bosses (the Oblivion Gate Warden, his crystals and host, the Abyss Dungeon's Remnant, Elite Breach foes and arena opponents). It lands the biggest blow the fight allows instead of nothing, and spell damage numbers on these bosses show what can actually land.

Damage-over-time spells keep burning on those online bosses (not arena opponents) and the sea serpent instead of stopping after their first hit. Recasting refreshes the effect rather than stacking it.
Chain Lightning, Earthshaker and Dragonfire now show their own damage numbers, tagged with the power's name.
The Elite Breach Gauntlet's caster plates now glow gold on their pillars and dim once that caster is silenced, and the objective names both ways to silence a caster: hold its plate, or slay it.
In a duel, your health bar now shows your duel vitality and drops when your opponent hits you. It goes back to your real health when the duel ends; duels still never touch your real health.
Furniture in a player's home or yard, and a mountain, camp or town that loads in around you, no longer trap you. They appear, you walk out, and they turn solid once you're clear.

Dungeon lifts and moving floors no longer trap you or push you out of the map. A lift that meets your head waits until you step clear, and a lowering floor stops above you. If you ever fall out of a dungeon, you're returned to its entrance.

Find me on the town map now takes you to where you're standing, zooms to your street and marks you with the red cross, instead of jumping to the edge of town. On the dungeon map it also brings you back to your own floor.

Find me on the town map now takes you to where you're standing, zooms to your street and marks you with the red cross, instead of jumping to the edge of town. On the dungeon map it also brings you back to your own floor.

At a guild's Buy Spells counter, a purchase the shop refuses now tells you why (no spellbook, or not enough gold) instead of doing nothing. The message goes away with a click, and Leave works on the next press.
A guild or coven whose quest you haven't finished now says so and names that quest, instead of "That service is not available yet."
Worn items that make you invisible, blending or a shade no longer stay switched off after you land a blow. The effect comes back on its own within six game hours while the item is still worn.
Catching a disease now shows an "Unwell" tile on the Enhanced HUD and "You feel unwell." in the Status box while it incubates. The disease's name appears once its symptoms begin.
The Enchanting Station now lists crafted pieces too small to give Arcane Essence, greaves and pauldrons among them, grayed out with the reason: a piece needs 100 enchantment points for one Essence.
Revenants no longer take your horse, cart, deeds or spellbook. Anything one took before comes back to your pack the next time you load, and you'll be told.

An heir can now reach the remains of an ancestor who died inside another player's instance. Where the shared dungeon is laid smaller, its door offers you an instance of your own, and the remains lie where they fell.

Characters left with negative gold by the old large-sale bug (fixed in 0.0.249) can now be repaired by staff: the gold is reset, what you were owed comes back as a letter of credit, and the trading freeze the bad sale caused is lifted. Contact staff if this happened to you.
Gathering, the Notice Board's writs and traders, town yards, the guild chapters and the arena board ask far less of the account database, so they answer quickly in the evening rush.
When the account service is slow, your game now waits a moment before asking for display data again instead of asking harder. Gathering, crafting, trading and saving are never held back.

Abyss Dungeons stopped appearing when most players online were at sea. A new one now always rises by a town. If players are crowded at sea, it goes to the busiest region on land, or to one of the Bay's great cities.
An Abyss Dungeon that already rose "at sea" before this update now shows up by one of the Bay's great cities, so you don't have to wait for it to fade.

Two new tiles beside the Renown bar: Skills ready (left) counts the skills a rest or a journey would raise; Firmament stars (right) counts the stars and craft points you haven't placed yet. Click the stars to open the Firmament page. Both can be moved with Alt+U.
Hover any buff, debuff, need or disease tile to see what it does, in the same card the inventory uses.
Under DFO Grimoire, the level-up notes are now written in full, readable ink.
A new Lantern slot, after the Crystals. A lantern placed there hangs at your belt, is lit while it hangs, and goes out when you take it off.
New Monster Volume setting (0-100%) under Audio. It controls monster calls, attack sounds and pain cries.
Monsters call 60% less often. The city watch and companions are unchanged.

Clicking an NPC that a quest is waiting on now shows the quest's message and reward right away. The talk window, guild or shop opens after them, instead of the quest words appearing only after you pressed Exit.
The window no longer changes size when you switch pages. The page list always sits on the left, with a short description under each entry.
The Level page opens on a card showing your level.
Mastery bars are now thin red bars, the same height as the yellow ones.
The World Map has a Players filter (Shown / Hidden). It shares its setting with the Overworld's Travellers switch.
The female hooded armour no longer floats over the shoulders, and the mace head is no longer pale and black.
The female hooded armour no longer floats over the shoulders, and the mace head is no longer pale and black.
Kamer & Kab's Daggerfall Enemy Expansion 1.3.4 is in the Mods pane and is on by default. Online, the room's setting applies to everyone in it.
The mod's fifty new enemies are registered, with their art. While the mod is on, its changes to sixteen classic monsters and two classic classes apply, and quests can name the new enemies.

The new enemies animate and stand at the size the mod gives them. Their glowing parts glow, and their spirits are drawn see-through, in dungeons, in towns and in the Overworld's bands. Female riders and Dark Slayers fall as their own female corpses, and the Hell Hound's corpse burns on outside dungeons too.

The new enemies now turn up in the world: every dungeon type, the water, and each climate's towns by night, wilderness by day and wilderness by night use the mod's encounter tables. Laboratories pick one of two tables each, the same one every visit and for every player. Arriving in a town by fast travel or a load picks that climate's town-night table, as in Daggerfall Unity.

The new enemies cast their own spells. The mod's four new spells join the spell list and are hidden from shops, as in Daggerfall Unity. Each spellcaster casts its own book: King Lysandus his Bolt of Vengeance, the spellcasting classes by their level.

The new enemies' attacks carry their effects: The Blood Spider's bite leeches blood. The Gloom Wraith's touch silences. The Fire Daemon's touch burns. The Will-o'-wisp's touch wracks. The lizard men paralyse like a spider. The bat and the ghouls carry disease. The nymph tires you.

Blunt weapons do half damage to the Skeletal Soldier and silver does double, as against the Skeletal Warrior. While the mod is on, Barbarians no longer take that rule, as in the mod. Each new enemy has its own kind (beast, humanoid, undead, daedra) for racial bonuses, Detect, Dispel and Pacify, and its own language.

The Troll gets back up. Ten seconds after it falls, a new Troll stands where the body lay, unless a spell's missile burns the body to ash first. Fire is the Troll's weakness; blades and arrows do nothing to the body. The body can't be searched. A Troll still down when you save keeps its time on load, and a burnt one stays burnt, after a reload and for a player who arrives later. The mod's "Disable Troll Respawn" setting keeps them down. Online, every player sees the same body rise or burn.

With Morrowind attached, the new enemies stand in Morrowind's bodies where Morrowind has the same creature: the Goblin, the wolves, the Troll, the Boar, the Mudcrab, the Ogre, the Dremora Churl, the golems, the ghouls, the Scamp, the Dwemer centurions, the Skeletal Soldier and the ghosts (seen through). The lizard men stand as Argonians, and the new classes as people. The riders, the flyers and the creatures Morrowind lacks keep their Daggerfall sprites.
With Roleplay & Realism: Items' realistic enemy equipment on, the mod kits every class enemy, the classic classes included:
The new classes are armed as the class they are drawn from: a Knight Rider fights as a Knight, a Druid as a Mage, a Bounty Hunter as an Assassin (with the Assassin's chance of a poisoned blade).
Class enemies wear their second weapon.

Armour follows what each class may wear. With Roleplay & Realism: Items' new armour on, a class that may not wear plate sometimes wears the chain or leather set instead. A Monk wears about half the armour it did, and Rangers and Burglars wear their classic pieces rather than chain or leather.
In There's a Hole in the Bottom of the Ocean's abyss, the new classes are treated as monsters, as that mod's own code does.
Fix: the vampires, the ancient vampires, the frost and fire daedra and the fire atronach no longer cast shadows, sprite or Morrowind body, as in Daggerfall Unity.
Fix: with realistic enemy equipment, an enemy no longer holds a two-handed weapon and a shield at once, and an orc's poisoned blade is rolled before its gear turns orcish, as in Daggerfall Unity.
The mod's pictures leave memory once drawn.
The new enemies' names are translated into every language the game offers. Before this, they showed in English everywhere, as in Daggerfall Unity.

With both mods on (the default, and always online), Meaner Monsters plays as MUDEX, the version its author Ralzar made for Daggerfall Enemy Expansion. Meaner Monsters itself asks players to make this switch.
MUDEX sets the health, damage, level and armour of 35 monsters, classic and new. The Grizzly Bear now hits for 1-20 with 50-100 health, and the Goblin for 4-15.
Every dungeon type gets themed encounter tables that don't scale with your level, beside its usual one. A crypt might be a lich's, a vampire's, a mummy's, a necromancer's or a haunted one.

The game no longer distorts when many loud sounds play at once. A limiter now sits on the final output, so the Legion-Lord's heavy blows, his roars and the gate music can't push the mix past full volume. Everyday sound is unchanged.
Hellfire, Meteor, Brand and Torment play at most two copies of their sound, instead of one per targeted player. In a group, a third-phase Hellfire played ten copies at once.
Inside the gate, other players' sounds play 4 dB quieter, as they already do in the Elite Gates Spire, so the boss's warnings stand out.
The gate fight's spark, meteor, crystal and portal effects are prepared as you arrive in the court, instead of the first time each appears mid-fight.
The monsters a gate can field are loaded as you arrive, instead of when the first wave rises or the boss splits in two.
Blood splashes no longer redo their image work on every hit.
With Enhanced Lighting shadows on, the brief flashes of the boss's landings, his fall and the Wrath no longer cast shadows, so they no longer force shadow redraws.

Severide is the first ever to take Redoubt 10 of the Battlespire, alone, in 1:17:40. He now holds the First of the Spire title and its aura, Firstlight. Equip them from your profile. A letter from the Developers waits in the mailbox.

Firstlight is now a one-of-a-kind aura, worn only by the first company ever to take Redoubt 10. A dial of the ten Redoubts lights round the wearer's feet one after another, and ten spires of dawn-light rise as each is taken. When the tenth falls, the dawn breaks: a sunburst runs out across the ground and a shaft of first light rises past the head.

The First of the Spire title and its aura, Firstlight, now go to Serveride (seen in the world as Severide), the first ever to take Redoubt 10 of the Battlespire. The last update had named the wrong account, so nobody received them.

Herbs, veins, boulders, trees and fishing schools no longer wear a coloured outline. They catch the light instead: small star-shaped glints flash on the node itself and fade, and from a distance a soft sheen of light passes over it now and then.
The node you're working goes quiet: no glints and no sheen while you pick, mine, chop or skin it, so the Basket's and the Pick-Axe's own glints are the only ones to watch.
Glints stay on the spot of the plant, vein or tree they belong to as you walk; they no longer hop about.
Walls and rocks in front of a node hide its glint, and fog and the sea's murk fade it as they fade the node.
With reduced motion turned on in your system, the glints hold still and no sheen crosses.

The glints follow the light where the node stands. They are bright in daylight and dim at night, underground and in a storm, but never so dim you can't find the node. A node beside a lamp in a mine catches its light.
Gathering nodes behind you no longer cost a full-screen pass each frame.
The first live event, from 20 October to 7 November.

Killing foes, gathering, crafting, fishing, winning tavern games, finishing quests and bounties, sailing, the endgame and holding a fallen star can all earn you Soul Cakes. They go straight into your pack.
Every find is doubled on All Hallows' Eve, 31 October, and on the in-game 13th of Frostfall and 3rd of Hearthfire, when the dead walk (about an hour of real time each).
The Wyrd's Raiment: a nine-piece Aetheric set: eight leather pieces, so casters can wear it, and the Witchmoon Athame. Its set bonuses are Wyrd-Sight, Tallow-Ward and Soul Harvest.
Witchwarden: a title.
Witchfire: an aura of green fire and tallow candles.
Profile icons: a new kind of cosmetic, worn in your portrait instead of your face and seen by other players. Three to buy, one to earn.
Six festival cards for the Iliac Hand, including the legendary King Lysandus' Spectre.

Every town is decorated in its own region's style: turnip lanterns and straw effigies in High Rock; candles and bowls of fire in Hammerfell; bonfires and horned skulls in the mountains; ward-staves in the fens; bones in the Haunted Woodlands
Set a Hearth Offering out at the door of your home and fill it with Soul Cakes.
Other players can take one cake from each offering per day.
You can take your offering back in at any time, even after the festival. You get back the bowl and every cake still in it.
When other players have taken 25 cakes from your offerings, you earn the Hearthkeeper title.
Take 10 cakes from other players' offerings to earn the Soul Cake icon.
Every real hour is a night. Each night one of the Bay's twelve covens pulls three stars down into the wilds of its region, each near a different town.
A new star burns in the sky for a minute and a half before it falls. Chat names the town it is falling toward, and the map, the compass and the Timers window point to it.
When it lands, hold it. The coven comes in four waves, then their master. What they summon goes for the star itself, and if its light runs out, the coven takes it.
The master calls a circle twice. While any of the circle stands, the master takes only a quarter of every blow. Break the circle first.
An unheld star is lost 15 minutes after it falls.
On the 13th of Frostfall, the night's last star is the Heart-Star. Its master's circle is twice the size, and so are its rewards.
A held star gives Renown, 30 silver, gold, 1 to 3 pieces of Starfall Glass, a magic item or better, and Soul Cakes. Your account card counts your Stars held.
Starfall Glass is pale glass that still holds some of the star's light. It stacks, and any merchant pays well for it.
One star in four also gives a piece of the Starspun Weave, Mephala's nine-piece set. The Heart-Star always gives one.

2 pieces, Spinner's Thread: poison resistance and Agility. 4 pieces, Bound in Silk: every 4th full-weight weapon hit on the same enemy deals 60 to 140% more damage. 6 pieces, Mephala's Veil: a hit that drops you below 30% health gives you Chameleon for 10 seconds. It recovers in 4 minutes.

A new festival questline from Morwen, a Wyrd Sister of Glenmoril. It opens at level 6, online with a registered account, while the festival runs. A Wyrd Sister hands you Morwen's letter, or her raven brings it if you hold a star first.
Hold a fallen star, face the Coven on the Bluff, then hold three more stars to earn the title Starwarden and 30 Soul Cakes. The Wyrd Sisters' window shows the title once you hold it.
Holding the Heart-Star during Three Stars is an optional objective: it pays more and adds Morwen's Heart-Star Ring to your choice of reward.
At the end, decide what becomes of the Spinner's spindle: burn it in Hircine's fire, sell it to the Mages Guild, or take it to a priest of Arkay at Arkay's own temple. Each choice has its own reward.
The compass on the Enhanced HUD now shows the Sea Serpent and a found Abyss Dungeon. Both marks were being dropped before they reached it.
Interacting in a town where a player has set out a Hearth Offering no longer crashes the game. The crash happened whatever you interacted with there: a body, a door or a person.
In those towns the names under your crosshair show again, and Hearth Offerings work: take a Soul Cake from someone else's, or fill or take in your own.
Questline letters no longer arrive in a heap. Each new questline's opening letter now waits until the last one has reached you, and an hour of your character's time after it.
A quest giver placed in a Mages Guild hall no longer stands inside the guild's own quest-giver.
When a townsperson marks a building on your map, you can now see it from the world map too. In a town, the world map has a tab for the town's streets.
On a crowded town map, a name with no room is drawn as a star. Pointing at the star shows the building's name, so a marked building always shows.
Trees in towns no longer grow around fountains, wells and crates. A tree that stands close to one is drawn smaller.
Raw Fish in your Materials Bag can be cooked over a fire. The cooked fish goes into your pack.
The joinery's carpenter, signboard and workbench all open the workbench with its craft buttons. Before, the carpenter and the signboard opened it with the Workbench marked as away.
Putting your goods in the Stores no longer locks the buttons for a long time. Everything you put in at once is saved once, not once a material.
Temper at the Anvil and Temper at the Loom are back on the Stores page.
After a journey across the sea, your ship stops instead of rowing on by itself. This happened when you left the helm on oars, without full sails.
Port towns along the coast that had no harbour now have one, including Daggerfall, Sentinel and Wayrest. A harbour can stand a little way from its town where the shore lies far out.
Sailing from one port to another now counts at every port, so the Under Sail tutorial completes.
You can't go below to your ship's cabin while enemies are nearby. Before, going below made pirates vanish.

The Overworld now shows the land out to the horizon. The haze over sunny and cloudy skies used to close a few kilometres out, leaving one pale wash. It now thins out to where the land meets the sky, and you can tilt the camera up to look along it (down to 15 degrees, from 30).
Clouds' shadows now carry on out to the far hills, with no straight edge where they used to stop.
You can click on land you can see in the distance to travel there. Before, distant land answered "That lies beyond what you can see from here."
While nearby land is still loading, distant hills fill the gap instead of open sky.

Loading into the world does less work. The longest freeze while the world is built is about half as long, and the first moments in the world freeze less often: the map of Tamriel is fitted in a fraction of the time, and the roads' travellers are planned faster, thanks to joaomdb3's TRIP-PICKS (#854), carried here.

Trading with a large inventory is smooth. A shop or a trade with another player now opens with its item pictures in place, instead of rebuilding the window once per picture for up to minutes. A click on an item answers in about 50 ms where it took up to 0.8 s, and buying or selling a piece takes about 0.1 s where it took up to 3 s. Long lists keep their place while you scroll, whatever the height of each row.

No more freezes while shaders compile. Oblivion Gates (the gate's fire, its veil, the court's telegraphs, blows, crystals and portal), the Elite Gates' fight, the glint on gathering nodes, the sea's effects, spell impacts and the snow on the ground now compile in the background. Before, the game froze for each one, for seconds on some graphics cards. Each effect appears a moment later instead. On most graphics cards, the gate and node effects now start compiling while you load in.

The weather's snow no longer eats your frame rate. While the snow on the ground was catching up with the weather (after arriving somewhere, or travelling on), it cost about 18 ms a frame and spiked past 60 ms. It now keeps to its 3 ms, and the snowline settles in over a few seconds instead.

If you were the only one who entered the breach, the Discord announcement of a tenth Redoubt (10, 20, 30...) now names you and says you did it alone. For example: *Mara took Redoubt 20 of the Battlespire (Hall 100) alone in 40:00, from Redoubt 10*. Before, it said *"Mara's company took..."* however many people were in the breach.

A group is still announced as a company. Anyone who stepped through with you counts, even if they fell, went home or left. The announcement now names someone who actually went in, never an opener who stayed outside.
Once the first hall wakes, the company tracker counts only the people who came in. A party member who was called but never stepped through no longer shows as part of your company.

In an Athenaeum, the Orrery's six stones now stand in the hall. Each has a dial, a hand showing its hour, and two levers: the right lever turns the stone forward, the left turns it back. Before, each stone was a gold ring on the floor, and you had to search the empty air beside it to find the turn.

The door at the end of a span no longer stays shut when you stop to time your jumps. Standing still without moving the mouse made the Spire lose sight of your crossing, and the door would not open for you.
If the door won't let you through, it now tells you why and what to do.

Damage numbers on Spire lords and enemies now show the damage each hit actually did, a moment after it lands. Before, they showed what the hit would do to an ordinary enemy, which can be far more than a lord takes. The numbers now add up to the fight's damage chart. Damage over time and Arcane Echo repeats show their numbers too, and a follow-up blow (Open Hand, Many Endings) is counted in its blow's number rather than popping a second one.

Changing a class skill on the Growth tab could be repeated to push your level far past what any class can reach. One class reached level 223. A skill's training now leaves your class with it. Your level and its progress still never drop, but after you give up a trained skill for a less trained one, your class skills make up the difference before your next level comes any closer.
The swap form now tells you how many points that is, beside the picks and again when it asks you to confirm.
